sentences.zh: 顯宗諸子

translations.literal: Sons of Xianzong
translations.idiomatic: Sons of Emperor Xianzong

sentences.zh: 顯宗孝懿皇后生章宗，昭聖皇后生宣宗，諸姬田氏生鄆王琮、瀛王瑰、霍王從彝，劉氏生瀛王從憲，王氏生溫王玠。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoyi of Xianzong bore Zhangzong; Empress Zhaosheng bore Xuanzong. Among the concubines, Lady Tian bore the Prince of Yun, Cong, the Prince of Ying, Gui, and the Prince of Huo, Cong Yi; Lady Liu bore the Prince of Ying, Cong Xian; Lady Wang bore the Prince of Wen, Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong's Empress Xiaoyi gave birth to Zhangzong, and Empress Zhaosheng to Xuanzong. Of his lesser consorts, Lady Tian was mother to Prince Cong of Yun, Prince Gui of Ying, and Prince Cong Yi of Huo; Lady Liu to Prince Cong Xian of Ying; and Lady Wang to Prince Jie of Wen.

sentences.zh: 鄆王琮，本名承慶，母田氏，其後封裕陵充華。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yun, Cong, original name Chengqing, mother Lady Tian; she was later enfeoffed as Chonghua of Yuling Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cong of Yun, whose birth name was Chengqing, was born to Lady Tian, who was later granted the title Chonghua of Yuling Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 琮儀觀豐偉，機警清辯，性寬厚，好學。

translations.literal: Cong's bearing was imposing and handsome; he was quick-witted and clear in debate, of generous character, and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Cong cut a striking figure—tall and handsome, alert and articulate in debate. He was generous by nature and devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 世宗選進士之有名行者納坦謀嘉教之，女直小字及漢字皆通習。

translations.literal: Shizong selected the renowned jinshi graduate Natan Moujia to instruct him, and he mastered both Jurchen script and Chinese characters.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong appointed the distinguished jinshi Natan Moujia as his tutor, and Cong became proficient in both the Jurchen script and Chinese writing.

sentences.zh: 及長，輕財好施，無慍色，善吟詠，不喜聞人過，至於騎射繪塑之藝，皆造精妙。

translations.literal: When grown, he was free with money and generous in giving, never showing anger, skilled at versifying, and disliking to hear of others' faults. As for the arts of horsemanship, archery, painting, and sculpture, he attained exquisite mastery in all.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he was liberal with wealth and quick to give, never showing a cross face. He was adept at poetry and disliked hearing others' faults spoken. In horsemanship, archery, painting, and sculpture alike he achieved remarkable skill.

sentences.zh: 大定十八年，封道國公。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Dading, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dao State.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 18 he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dao.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，加崇進。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, he was promoted to Chongjin rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was raised to the Chongjin noble rank.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，遷開府儀同三司，封鄆王。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong took the throne, he was transferred to Defender-in-chief with equal protocol to the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed as Prince of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong acceded, Cong was promoted to Defender-in-chief with equal protocol to the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed as Prince of Yun.

sentences.zh: 明昌元年，授婆速路獲火羅合打世襲猛安，留京師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Mingchang, he was granted the hereditary meng'an of Pasu Circuit Huo Luo Hedá and remained at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 1 he was granted the hereditary meng'an of Huo Luo Hedá in Pasu Circuit and remained at the capital.

sentences.zh: 五年，薨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died.

sentences.zh: 上輟朝，親臨奠於殯所。

translations.literal: The emperor suspended court and personally came to offer libations at the mourning hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended court and came in person to offer libations at the mourning hall.

sentences.zh: 諡曰莊靖，改莊惠。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Zhuangjing, later changed to Zhuanghui.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Zhuangjing, later revised to Zhuanghui.

sentences.zh: 瀛王瑰，本名桓篤，鄆王琮之同母弟也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ying, Gui, original name Huandu, was the uterine younger brother of the Prince of Yun, Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gui of Ying, birth name Huandu, was Prince Cong of Yun's younger brother by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 重厚寡言，內行修飭，工詩，精於騎射、書藝、女直大小字。

translations.literal: He was grave and taciturn, scrupulous in private conduct, accomplished in poetry, and expert in horsemanship and archery, calligraphy, and both large and small Jurchen script.
translations.idiomatic: He was grave and sparing of speech, meticulous in private conduct, skilled in poetry, and accomplished in horsemanship, archery, calligraphy, and both forms of Jurchen writing.

sentences.zh: 大定二十二年，封崇國公。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Dading, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Chong State.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 22 he was enfeoffed as Duke of Chong.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，加崇進。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, he was promoted to Chongjin rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was raised to the Chongjin noble rank.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，遷開府儀同三司，封瀛王。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong took the throne, he was transferred to Defender-in-chief with equal protocol to the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed as Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong acceded, Gui was promoted to Defender-in-chief with equal protocol to the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed as Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 明昌三年，薨。

translations.literal: In the third year of Mingchang he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 3 he died.

sentences.zh: 敕葬事所須皆從官給，命工部侍郎胥持國等典喪事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that all funeral needs be supplied from official stores, and Vice Minister of Works Xu Chiguo and others were appointed to oversee the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decreed that all funeral expenses be met from official funds and appointed Vice Minister of Works Xu Chiguo and others to manage the obsequies.

sentences.zh: 比葬，帝三臨奠，哭之慟。

translations.literal: By the time of burial, the emperor had come three times to offer libations and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Before the burial was complete the emperor had come three times to offer libations, weeping bitterly each time.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文敬。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 其後帝謂輔臣曰：「王性忠孝，兄弟中最為善人，故朕嘗令在左右。

translations.literal: Later the emperor said to his chief ministers: "The prince was by nature loyal and filial, the finest man among his brothers, and for that reason I often kept him at my side.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor told his chief ministers, "The prince was loyal and filial by nature—the best of his brothers—and that is why I so often kept him near me.

sentences.zh: 溫王雖幼，亦佳。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wen, though young, was also excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jie of Wen, though still young, was splendid too.

sentences.zh: 不二旬俱逝，良可哀悼。」

translations.literal: Within less than twenty days both passed away—truly a cause for mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Yet within twenty days both were gone. It is deeply to be mourned."

sentences.zh: 瀛王從憲，本名吾里不，母劉氏，後封裕陵茂儀。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ying, Cong Xian, original name Wulibu, mother Lady Liu; she was later enfeoffed as Maoyi of Yuling Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cong Xian of Ying, birth name Wulibu, was born to Lady Liu, who was later granted the title Maoyi of Yuling Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 大定二十六年，賜名琦。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Dading, he was granted the name Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 26 he was given the name Qi.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，加開府儀同三司，封壽王。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong took the throne, he was promoted to Defender-in-chief with equal protocol to the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed as Prince of Shou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong acceded, he was promoted to Defender-in-chief with equal protocol to the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed as Prince of Shou.

sentences.zh: 承安元年，以郊祀恩進封英。

translations.literal: In the first year of Cheng'an, by grace of the suburban sacrifice he was advanced to Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In Cheng'an 1, on account of the suburban sacrifice amnesty, he was advanced to Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 四年，改封瀛。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, his fief was changed to Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year his fief was changed to Ying.

sentences.zh: 泰和五年，更賜今名。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe, he was again granted his present name.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 5 he was granted his present name Cong Xian.

sentences.zh: 六年，授秘書監。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was appointed Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 八年，薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died.

sentences.zh: 從憲風儀秀峙，性寬厚，善騎射，待府僚以禮，秩滿去者皆有贐。

translations.literal: Cong Xian's bearing was elegant and outstanding; he was generous by nature, skilled in horsemanship and archery, treated his household staff with courtesy, and all who completed their terms of service received parting gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Cong Xian was graceful in bearing and generous in temperament, skilled in horsemanship and archery. He treated his household officers with courtesy, and everyone who completed a term of service left with a parting gift.

sentences.zh: 帝尤愛重，初以病聞，即臨問之，賜錢五百萬。

translations.literal: The emperor cherished him especially. As soon as word of his illness came, he went in person to inquire after him and granted five million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored him above all. At the first report of illness he went in person to inquire after him and granted five million in cash.

sentences.zh: 還宮，詔府僚上其疾增損狀，仍敕門司夜一鼓即奏，比五更重言之。

translations.literal: Returning to the palace, he ordered the household staff to submit reports on whether his illness had worsened or improved, and further commanded the gate office to memorialize at the first night watch, repeating the report at the fifth watch.
translations.idiomatic: Back at the palace he ordered the prince's household to submit daily reports on whether his condition had worsened or improved, and commanded the gate office to memorialize at the first night watch and again at the fifth.

sentences.zh: 及薨，上哭之慟，為輟朝臨奠者再。

translations.literal: When he died, the emperor wept bitterly and twice suspended court to come in person to offer libations.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the emperor wept bitterly and twice suspended court to offer libations in person.

sentences.zh: 諭旨判大睦親府事宛王永升曰：「瀛王家事，叔宜規畫。

translations.literal: An edict instructed Wan Yong Sheng, who oversaw the Great Office of Imperial Kinship, saying: "As for the Prince of Ying's household affairs, Uncle should take charge of planning them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed Wan Yong Sheng, overseer of the Great Office of Imperial Kinship: "You, Uncle, should take charge of the Prince of Ying's household affairs.

sentences.zh: 聞其二姬方孕，若生子，即以付之。」

translations.literal: I hear his two consorts are pregnant; if they bear sons, entrust them to him at once."
translations.idiomatic: I hear his two consorts are with child; if they bear sons, entrust the children to him at once."

sentences.zh: 以右宣徽使移剌都護其喪葬，斂以內庫之服，其餘所須，亦從官給。

translations.literal: The Right Xuanhui Commissioner Yila Du was assigned to oversee his funeral. He was dressed in robes from the inner treasury; all other needs were likewise supplied from official stores.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Xuanhui Commissioner Yila Du was assigned to oversee the funeral. The prince was dressed in robes from the inner treasury, and all other needs were met from official funds as well.

sentences.zh: 諡曰敦懿。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Dunyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Dunyi.

sentences.zh: 溫王玠，本名謀良虎，母王氏，後封裕陵婉儀。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wen, Jie, original name Mou Lianghu, mother Lady Wang; she was later enfeoffed as Wanyi of Yuling Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jie of Wen, birth name Mou Lianghu, was born to Lady Wang, who was later granted the title Wanyi of Yuling Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 玠幼穎秀，性溫厚，好學。

translations.literal: Jie was precocious and refined in youth, gentle and generous in character, and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Jie was bright and graceful, gentle by nature, and devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 大定二十九年，章宗即位，加開府儀同三司，封溫王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Dading, when Zhangzong took the throne, he was promoted to Defender-in-chief with equal protocol to the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed as Prince of Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 29, when Zhangzong acceded, Jie was promoted to Defender-in-chief with equal protocol to the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed as Prince of Wen.

sentences.zh: 明昌三年，薨，年十一。

translations.literal: In the third year of Mingchang he died, aged eleven.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 3 he died, aged eleven.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，上為輟朝，親臨奠哭之。

translations.literal: When word of his death arrived, the emperor suspended court and came in person to offer libations and weep.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death arrived the emperor suspended court and came in person to offer libations and weep.

sentences.zh: 諡曰悼敏。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Daomin.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Daomin.

sentences.zh: 章宗諸子

translations.literal: Sons of Zhangzong
translations.idiomatic: Sons of Emperor Zhangzong

sentences.zh: 章宗欽懷皇后生絳王洪裕，資明夫人林氏生荊王洪靖，諸姬生榮王洪熙、英王洪衍、壽王洪輝。

translations.literal: Empress Qinhuai of Zhangzong bore the Prince of Jiang, Hong Yu; Lady Ziming of the Lin clan bore the Prince of Jing, Hong Jing; among the concubines were born the Prince of Rong, Hong Xi, the Prince of Ying, Hong Yan, and the Prince of Shou, Hong Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhangzong's Empress Qinhuai gave birth to Prince Hong Yu of Jiang; Lady Ziming of the Lin clan to Prince Hong Jing of Jing; and of his lesser consorts came Prince Hong Xi of Rong, Prince Hong Yan of Ying, and Prince Hong Hui of Shou.

sentences.zh: 元妃李氏生葛王忒鄰。

translations.literal: Primary Consort Lady Li bore the Prince of Ge, Te Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Primary Consort Lady Li gave birth to Prince Te Lin of Ge.

sentences.zh: 洪裕，大定二十六年生。

translations.literal: Hong Yu was born in the twenty-sixth year of Dading.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Yu was born in Dading 26.

sentences.zh: 是時顯宗薨逾年，世宗深感，及聞皇曾孫生，喜甚。

translations.literal: At that time it was more than a year since Xianzong's death, and Shizong was still deeply grieved; when he heard that a great-grandson had been born, he was overjoyed.
translations.idiomatic: It was more than a year since Emperor Xianzong's death, and Shizong still mourned deeply; when he heard a great-grandson had been born, he was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 滿三月，宴于慶和殿，賜曾孫金鼎，金香合，重彩二十端，骨睹犀、吐鶻玉山子、兔兒垂頭一副，名馬二匹。

translations.literal: At the completion of three months, a banquet was held in Qinghe Hall, and the great-grandson was given a gold tripod, a gold incense box, twenty bolts of heavy brocade, a set of bone-dushi rhinoceros horn, a tuhu jade mountain ornament, and rabbit-fur hanging caps, and two famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: At his third month a banquet was held in Qinghe Hall, and the great-grandson received a gold tripod, a gold incense box, twenty bolts of heavy brocade, a set of bone-inlaid rhinoceros-horn fittings, a tuhu jade mountain ornament, rabbit-fur hanging caps, and two fine horses.

sentences.zh: 章宗進玉雙駝鎮紙、玉琵琶撥、玉鳳鉤、骨睹犀具佩刀、衣服一襲。

translations.literal: Zhangzong presented a jade double-camel paperweight, a jade pipa plectrum, a jade phoenix hook, a bone-dushi rhinoceros horn fitted belt knife, and a suit of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong presented a jade double-camel paperweight, a jade pipa plectrum, a jade phoenix hook, a rhinoceros-horn belt knife with bone inlay, and a suit of robes.

sentences.zh: 世宗禦酒歌歡，乙夜方罷。

translations.literal: Shizong himself poured wine and led the singing in celebration; the revelry did not end until the second watch of the night.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong poured wine himself and led the singing; the celebration did not end until well past midnight.

sentences.zh: 二十八年十月丙寅，薨。

translations.literal: On the bingyin day of the tenth month of the twenty-eighth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day of the tenth month of the twenty-eighth year he died.

sentences.zh: 明昌三年，追封絳王，賜名。

translations.literal: In the third year of Mingchang he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jiang and granted his name.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 3 he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jiang and granted the name Hong Yu.

sentences.zh: 洪靖，本名阿虎懶，明昌三年生。

translations.literal: Hong Jing, original name Ahulan, was born in the third year of Mingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Jing, birth name Ahulan, was born in Mingchang 3.

sentences.zh: 生而警秀，上所鍾愛。

translations.literal: From birth he was alert and refined, and the emperor cherished him dearly.
translations.idiomatic: From birth he was bright and graceful, and the emperor doted on him.

sentences.zh: 四年，薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died.

sentences.zh: 承安四年，追封荊王，賜名，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Cheng'an he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jing, granted his name, and promoted to Defender-in-chief with equal protocol to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In Cheng'an 4 he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jing, granted the name Hong Jing, and given the rank of Defender-in-chief with equal protocol to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 洪衍，本名撒改，明昌四年生，未幾薨。

translations.literal: Hong Yan, original name Sagai, was born in the fourth year of Mingchang and died not long after.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Yan, birth name Sagai, was born in Mingchang 4 and died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 承安四年，追封英王，賜名，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Cheng'an he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Ying, granted his name, and promoted to Defender-in-chief with equal protocol to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In Cheng'an 4 he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Ying, granted the name Hong Yan, and given the rank of Defender-in-chief with equal protocol to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 洪輝，本名訛論，承安二年五月生，彌月，封壽王。

translations.literal: Hong Hui, original name Elun, was born in the fifth month of the second year of Cheng'an; at his first full month he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Hui, birth name Elun, was born in the fifth month of Cheng'an 2; at his first full month he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shou.

sentences.zh: 閏六月壬午，病急風，募能醫者加宣武將軍，賜錢五百萬。

translations.literal: On the renwu day of the intercalary sixth month he fell ill with acute wind-stroke; whoever could cure him was to be promoted to General of Manifest Martiality and granted five million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day of the intercalary sixth month he fell ill with acute wind-stroke; anyone who could cure him was promised promotion to General of Manifest Martiality and five million in cash.

sentences.zh: 甲申，疾愈，印《無量壽經》一萬卷報謝，衍慶宮作普天大醮七日，無奏刑名，仍禁屠宰。

translations.literal: On the jiashen day his illness abated. Ten thousand copies of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life were printed in thanks; at Yanqing Palace a universal great jiao was performed for seven days; no criminal cases were heard, and slaughter was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day he recovered. Ten thousand copies of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life were printed in thanksgiving; Yanqing Palace held a seven-day universal great jiao; criminal cases were not heard, and slaughter was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 十月丁亥，薨，備禮葬。

translations.literal: On the dinghai day of the tenth month he died and was buried with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the tenth month he died and was buried with full ceremonial honors.

sentences.zh: 忒鄰，泰和二年八月生。

translations.literal: Te Lin was born in the eighth month of the second year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Te Lin was born in the eighth month of Taihe 2.

sentences.zh: 上久無皇嗣，祈禱於郊、廟、衍慶宮、亳州太清宮，至是喜甚。

translations.literal: The emperor had long been without an heir and had prayed at the suburban altars, the ancestral temples, Yanqing Palace, and the Taiqing Palace at Bozhou; now he was overjoyed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long lacked an heir and had prayed at the suburban altars, the ancestral temples, Yanqing Palace, and the Taiqing Palace at Bozhou; he was overjoyed at last.

sentences.zh: 彌月，將加封，三等國號無愜上意者，念世宗在位最久，年最高，初封葛王，遂封為葛王。

translations.literal: At his first full month, when he was to receive enfeoffment, none of the third-rank state titles pleased the emperor. Recalling that Shizong had reigned longest and lived to the greatest age, and that his first enfeoffment had been Prince of Ge, he was therefore enfeoffed as Prince of Ge.
translations.idiomatic: At his first full month, when enfeoffment was due, none of the third-rank state titles satisfied the emperor. He recalled that Shizong had reigned longest and lived longest, and that his first title had been Prince of Ge—and so the infant was enfeoffed as Prince of Ge.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸酉，生滿百日，放僧道度牒三千道，設醮玄真觀，宴于慶和殿。

translations.literal: On the guiyou day of the twelfth month, when he had completed one hundred days of life, three thousand ordination certificates for monks and Daoists were issued, a jiao was performed at Xuanzhen Abbey, and a banquet was held in Qinghe Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day of the twelfth month, at his hundredth day, three thousand ordination certificates for monks and Daoists were issued, a jiao was held at Xuanzhen Abbey, and a banquet was given in Qinghe Hall.

sentences.zh: 百官用天壽節禮儀，進酒稱賀，三品以上進禮物。

translations.literal: The officials used the ceremonial of the Heavenly Longevity Festival, presented wine and offered congratulations, and those of third rank and above presented gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Officials followed the ceremonial of the Heavenly Longevity Festival, presented wine and offered congratulations, and those of third rank and above brought gifts.

sentences.zh: 泰和三年，薨。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 3 he died.

sentences.zh: 衛紹王子

translations.literal: Sons of Prince Shao of Wei
translations.idiomatic: Sons of Prince Shao of Wei

sentences.zh: 贊曰：章宗晚年，繼嗣不立，遂屬意衛紹王。

translations.literal: The commentator says: In Zhangzong's later years the succession was not settled, and he therefore turned his hopes to the Prince of Shao of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: In his later years Zhangzong had not settled the succession and therefore looked to Prince Shao of Wei.

sentences.zh: 衛紹歷年不永，諸子凡禁錮二十餘年，鎬厲王諸子禁錮四十餘年，長女鰥男皆不得婚嫁。

translations.literal: Prince Shao of Wei's reign was brief; his sons were confined for more than twenty years in all. The sons of Prince Li of Hao were confined for more than forty years; grown daughters and unmarried sons were none of them permitted to marry.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shao of Wei's reign was short, and his sons were confined for more than twenty years altogether. The sons of Prince Li of Hao were confined for more than forty years; grown daughters and unmarried sons alike were denied marriage.

sentences.zh: 天興初，方弛其禁，金亡祚後可知矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxing the restrictions were only then relaxed; when Jin perished, what became of the imperial line afterward may be inferred.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the beginning of Tianxing were the restrictions eased; when the Jin fell, what became of the imperial line afterward needs little saying.

sentences.zh: 宣宗三子

translations.literal: Three sons of Xuanzong
translations.idiomatic: Three sons of Emperor Xuanzong

sentences.zh: 莊獻太子，名守忠，宣宗長子也。

translations.literal: The Zhuangxian Crown Prince, named Shouzhong, was the eldest son of Xuanzong.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhuangxian, named Shouzhong, was Emperor Xuanzong's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 其母未詳，說在《王后傳》。

translations.literal: His mother is not recorded in detail; the account is in the "Biography of the Queen Consort."
translations.idiomatic: His mother is not identified here; the account appears in the Biography of the Queen Consort.

sentences.zh: 胡沙虎既廢衛王，時上未至，迎守忠入居東宮。

translations.literal: After Hushahu had deposed the Prince of Wei, the emperor had not yet arrived; Shouzhong was welcomed to take up residence in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After Hushahu deposed the Prince of Wei, before the emperor himself had arrived, Shouzhong was brought into the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 貞祐元年閏九月甲申，立為皇太子，詔曰：「朕以眇躬，嗣服景命，念祖宗之遺統，方夙夜以靡遑，將上以承九廟之靈，而下以系多方之望。

translations.literal: On the jiashen day of the intercalary ninth month of the first year of Zhenyou he was established as crown prince. The edict said: "We, in our slight person, have succeeded to the luminous mandate, mindful of the legacy left by our ancestors and striving day and night without respite, intending above to sustain the spirits of the nine temples and below to bind the hopes of the many realms.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day of the intercalary ninth month of Zhenyou 1 he was installed as crown prince. The edict read: "We, in our slight person, have succeeded to the luminous mandate. Mindful of our ancestors' legacy, we strive day and night without rest, intending above to sustain the spirits of the nine temples and below to answer the hopes of the realm.

sentences.zh: 皇太子守忠性秉溫良，地居長嫡，以次第言之，則宜升儲嗣，以典禮質之，則足愜群情，其立為皇太子。」

translations.literal: Crown Prince Shouzhong is by nature gentle and good, and by birth the eldest legitimate son. By order of succession he ought to be raised as heir, and by ritual propriety he fully satisfies the people's wishes. Let him be established as crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Shouzhong is gentle and good by nature and the eldest legitimate son. By order of succession he should be heir, and by ritual propriety he satisfies the people's wishes. Let him be established as crown prince."

sentences.zh: 十月己未，以鎮國上將軍。

translations.literal: On the jiwei day of the tenth month, [appointing] the Senior General of the State Defender
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day of the tenth month, [appointing] the Senior General of the State Defender

sentences.zh: 太子少保阿魯罕為太子少師。

translations.literal: Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent Aruhan as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent Aruhan as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 庚申，上遣諭曰：「朕宮中每事裁減，汝亦宜知時難，斟酌撙節也。」

translations.literal: On the gengshen day the emperor sent word, saying: "In the palace I am cutting back on every matter; you too should know the times are hard and practice careful economy."
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day the emperor sent word: "I am cutting back on every matter in the palace; you too should know how hard the times are and practice careful economy."

sentences.zh: 又謂曰：「時方多艱，每事當從貶損，吾已放宮人百餘矣，東宮無用者亦宜出之。

translations.literal: He also said: "The times are full of hardship; every matter should be reduced. I have already released more than a hundred palace women; those in the Eastern Palace who are not needed should likewise be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "These are difficult times; everything should be scaled back. I have already released more than a hundred palace women, and those in the Eastern Palace who are not needed should be dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 汝讀書人，必能知此也。」

translations.literal: You are a man of learning—you must surely understand this."
translations.idiomatic: You are a scholar—you must understand this."

sentences.zh: 二年四月，宣宗遷汴，留守中京。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year, Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian, and [Shouzhong] remained to guard Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian, and Shouzhong remained at Zhongjing as regent.

sentences.zh: 七月，召至汴。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was summoned to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was summoned to Bian.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，薨。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year he died.

sentences.zh: 上臨奠殯所凡四次。

translations.literal: The emperor came in person to offer libations at the mourning hall four times in all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person to the mourning hall to offer libations four times in all.

sentences.zh: 四月，葬迎朔門外五里。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he was buried five li outside the Yingshuo Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he was buried five li outside the Yingshuo Gate.

sentences.zh: 諡莊獻。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Zhuangxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Zhuangxian.

sentences.zh: 五月，立其子鏗為皇太孫，始二歲。

translations.literal: In the fifth month his son Keng was established as imperial great-grandson, then aged two.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month his son Keng, then only two years old, was established as imperial great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 十二月薨，四年正月，賜諡沖懷太孫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he died; in the first month of the fourth year he was granted the posthumous title Chonghuai Imperial Great-Grandson.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month; in the first month of the fourth year he was given the posthumous title Chonghuai Imperial Great-Grandson.

sentences.zh: 玄齡，或曰莊獻太子母弟，早卒，未封爵。

translations.literal: Xuanling—some say he was the uterine younger brother of the Zhuangxian Crown Prince; he died young and received no enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling—some say he was Crown Prince Zhuangxian's younger brother by the same mother; he died young and was never enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 或曰麗妃史氏所生。

translations.literal: Others say he was born to Consort Li of the Shi clan.
translations.idiomatic: Others hold that he was born to Consort Li of the Shi clan.

sentences.zh: 荊王守純，本名盤都，宣宗第二子也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jing, Shouchun, original name Pandou, was the second son of Xuanzong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shouchun of Jing, birth name Pandou, was Emperor Xuanzong's second son.

sentences.zh: 母曰真妃龐氏。

translations.literal: His mother was True Consort Lady Pang.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was True Consort Lady Pang.

sentences.zh: 貞祐元年，封濮王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyou he was enfeoffed as Prince of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 1 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Pu.

sentences.zh: 二年，為殿前都點檢兼侍衛親軍都指揮使，權都元帥。

translations.literal: In the second year he became Chief Inspector of the Palace Front and Concurrent Commander of the Imperial Guard, with acting authority as Commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he became Chief Inspector of the Palace Front and concurrent Commander of the Imperial Guard, with acting authority as commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 上諭帥府曰：「濮王年幼，公事殊未諳，卿等毋以朕子故不相規戒。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the command headquarters: "The Prince of Pu is young and quite unfamiliar with public affairs; you must not fail to counsel and admonish him simply because he is my son.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the command headquarters: "Prince Pu is young and still unfamiliar with public business; do not hold back counsel and admonition simply because he is my son.

sentences.zh: 凡見將校，令謙和接遇可也。」

translations.literal: Whenever you meet officers, have him receive them with humility and courtesy."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he meets officers, let him receive them with humility and courtesy."

sentences.zh: 三年，為樞密使。

translations.literal: In the third year he became Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜平章政事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 興定元年，授世襲東平府路三屯猛安。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingding he was granted the hereditary meng'an of the three garrisons of Dongping Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 1 he was granted the hereditary meng'an of the three garrisons of Dongping Circuit.

sentences.zh: 三年，以知管差除令史梁瓛，誤書轉運副使張正倫宣命，奏乞治罪。

translations.literal: In the third year, because the clerk in charge of appointments Liang Huan, a registrar, had mistakenly written the commission for Vice Transport Commissioner Zhang Zhenglun, he memorialized requesting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, because the appointments registrar Liang Huan had mistakenly drafted the commission for Vice Transport Commissioner Zhang Zhenglun, he memorialized asking that punishment be imposed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「令史有犯，宰臣自當治之，何必關朕耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When a clerk offends, the chief ministers ought to discipline him themselves—why must it concern me?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "When a clerk offends, you chief ministers ought to discipline him yourselves—why bring it to me?"

sentences.zh: 是年三月，進封英王。

translations.literal: In the third month of that year he was advanced to Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of that year he was advanced to Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 時監察禦史程震言其不法，宣宗切責，杖司馬及大奴尤不法者數人。

translations.literal: At that time Supervising Censor Cheng Zhen reported his unlawful conduct; Xuanzong sternly rebuked him and had several of the most lawless stewards and great slaves beaten.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Supervising Censor Cheng Zhen reported his misconduct; Xuanzong rebuked him sharply and had several of the most lawless stewards and chief slaves beaten.

sentences.zh: 四年九月，守純欲發丞相高琪罪，密召知案蒲鮮石魯剌、令史蒲察胡魯、員外郎王阿里謀之，且屬令勿泄，而石魯剌、胡魯輒以告都事僕散奴失不，奴失不白高琪。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year, Shouchun wished to expose the crimes of Chief Councilor Gao Qi. He secretly summoned Case Officer Puxian Shilula, Registrar Pucha Hulu, and Outer Office Attendant Wang Ali to plot with him, and charged them not to leak it; yet Shilula and Hulu at once reported it to Chief Clerk Pusan Nushibu, and Nushibu informed Gao Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year Shouchun wished to expose Chief Councilor Gao Qi's crimes. He secretly summoned Case Officer Puxian Shilula, Registrar Pucha Hulu, and Outer Office Attendant Wang Ali to plot with him and ordered them not to reveal it; yet Shilula and Hulu at once told Chief Clerk Pusan Nushibu, who informed Gao Qi.

sentences.zh: 及高琪伏誅，守純劾三人者洩密事，奴失不免死，除名，石魯剌、胡魯各杖七十，勒停。

translations.literal: When Gao Qi was executed, Shouchun impeached the three men for leaking the secret. Nushibu could not escape death and was struck from the rolls; Shilula and Hulu were each beaten seventy strokes and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Qi was executed, Shouchun impeached the three for leaking the secret. Nushibu could not escape death and was struck from the rolls; Shilula and Hulu were each beaten seventy strokes and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 元光二年三月壬子，上戒諭守純曰：「始吾以汝為相者，庶幾相輔，不至為人譏病耳。

translations.literal: On the renzi day of the third month of the second year of Yuanguang, the emperor admonished Shouchun, saying: "When I first made you chief minister, I hoped you would assist me so that I would not become a target of criticism.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the third month of the second year of Yuanguang the emperor admonished Shouchun: "When I first made you chief minister, I hoped you would assist me so that I would not become a target of criticism.

sentences.zh: 汝乃惟飲酒耽樂，公事漫不加省，何耶？

translations.literal: Yet you only drink wine and indulge in pleasure, paying no attention at all to public business—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you only drink and take your ease, paying no heed to public business—why?

sentences.zh: 吾常聞人言己過，雖自省無之，亦未敢容易去懷也。」

translations.literal: When I hear others speak of my faults, even if on reflection I find none, I still do not lightly dismiss the matter from my mind."
translations.idiomatic: When I hear others speak of my faults, even if reflection finds none, I still do not lightly dismiss it from my mind."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「吾所以責汝者，但以崇飲不事事之故，汝勿過慮，遂至奪權。

translations.literal: He also said: "The reason I reprove you is only that you drink too much and neglect your duties; do not worry excessively that I will strip you of power.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "I reprove you only because you drink too much and neglect your duties; do not fear so much that I will strip you of power.

sentences.zh: 今諸相皆老臣，每事與之商略，使無貽物議足矣。」

translations.literal: Now all the chief ministers are old officials; consult with them on every matter so that there is no occasion for public criticism—that is enough."
translations.idiomatic: All the chief ministers now are old officials; consult with them on every matter so there is no occasion for public criticism—that is enough."

sentences.zh: 天興初，守純府第產肉芝一株，高五寸許，色紅鮮可愛，既而枝葉津流，濡地成血，臭不可聞，鏟去複生者再。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxing, a fleshy lingzhi fungus grew in Shouchun's residence, about five inches high, bright red and lovely; afterward sap flowed from its branches and leaves, soaking the ground into blood with a stench beyond bearing. It was dug out twice and grew again.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianxing a fleshy lingzhi grew in Shouchun's mansion, about five inches tall, bright red and lovely; then sap flowed from branch and leaf, soaking the ground into blood with a stench unbearable. Twice it was dug out and grew again.

sentences.zh: 夜則房榻間群狐號鳴，秉燭逐捕則失所在。

translations.literal: At night foxes howled in packs between bed and couch; when torches were taken to hunt them, they vanished.
translations.idiomatic: At night foxes howled in packs in the bedchamber; when torches were taken to hunt them, they could not be found.

sentences.zh: 未幾，訛可出質，哀宗遷歸德。

translations.literal: Before long, Wo Ke went out as hostage, and Aizong moved the capital to Guide.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wo Ke went out as hostage, and Emperor Aizong moved the capital to Guide.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，崔立亂。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, the Cui Li rebellion broke out.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year the Cui Li rebellion broke out.

sentences.zh: 四月癸巳，守純及諸宗室皆死青城。

translations.literal: On the guisi day of the fourth month, Shouchun and all the imperial clansmen died at Qingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day of the fourth month Shouchun and all the imperial clansmen died at Qingcheng.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：《詩》雲：「天難忱斯，不易維王，天位殷適，使不挾四方。」

translations.literal: The commentator says: The Book of Songs says: "Heaven is hard to rely on; it is not easy to be king. The heavenly position of Yin was fitting, yet it could not embrace the four quarters."
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: The Book of Songs says, "Heaven is hard to rely on; it is not easy to be king. The heavenly position of Yin was fitting, yet it could not embrace the four quarters."

sentences.zh: 信哉！

translations.literal: How true!
translations.idiomatic: How true!

sentences.zh: 守忠立為太子，未幾而薨，其子鏗立，又薨，哀宗複乏嗣，豈非天乎。

translations.literal: Shouzhong was established as crown prince and died not long after; his son Keng was established and also died. Aizong again lacked an heir—was this not Heaven's will?
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong was made crown prince and died soon after; his son Keng was installed and died as well. Aizong again lacked an heir—was this not Heaven's will?

sentences.zh: 正大間，國勢日蹙，本支殆盡，哀宗尚且疏忌骨肉，非明惠之賢，荊王幾不能免，豈「宗子維城」之道哉！

translations.literal: During the Zhengda era, as the state's position daily tightened and the main line was nearly exhausted, Aizong still distrusted his kin. Had it not been for the worth of Empress Minghui, the Prince of Jing would scarcely have escaped—is this the way of "imperial sons as the city's ramparts"?
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengda, as the state daily weakened and the main line was nearly spent, Aizong still distrusted his kin. But for the worth of Empress Minghui, Prince Jing would scarcely have escaped—is this truly the way of "imperial sons as the city's ramparts"?

sentences.zh: 獨吉思忠

translations.literal: Duji Sizhong
translations.idiomatic: Duji Sizhong

sentences.zh: 獨吉思忠，本名千家奴。

translations.literal: Duji Sizhong, original name Qianjianu.
translations.idiomatic: Duji Sizhong, birth name Qianjianu.

sentences.zh: 明昌六年，為行省都事，累遷同簽樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Mingchang he was Regional Inspector of the Branch Secretariat; he was repeatedly promoted to Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 6 he was Regional Inspector of the Branch Secretariat and was repeatedly promoted to Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 承安三年，除興平軍節度使，改西北路招討使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Cheng'an he was appointed Military Commissioner of Xingping Circuit and then changed to Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Route.
translations.idiomatic: In Cheng'an 3 he was appointed Military Commissioner of Xingping Circuit, then changed to Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Route.

sentences.zh: 初，大定間修築西北屯戍，西自坦舌，東至胡烈麼，幾六百里。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the Dading era, frontier garrisons were built in the northwest, from Tanshe in the west to Huliemo in the east, nearly six hundred li in all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Dading era, frontier garrisons were built in the northwest from Tanshe in the west to Huliemo in the east, nearly six hundred li in all.

sentences.zh: 中間堡障，工役促迫，雖有牆隍，無女牆副堤。

translations.literal: Between them were fortified posts, but the work was rushed; though there were walls and moats, there were no parapets or secondary embankments.
translations.idiomatic: Between them stood fortified posts, but the work was rushed; though there were walls and moats, there were no parapets or secondary embankments.

sentences.zh: 思忠增繕，用工七十五萬，止用屯戍軍卒，役不及民。

translations.literal: Sizhong added repairs, using seven hundred fifty thousand work units, employing only frontier garrison troops so that the labor did not fall on the people.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong added repairs using seven hundred fifty thousand work units, employing only frontier garrison troops so the labor did not fall on the people.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其勞，賜詔獎諭曰：「直乾之維，扼邊之要，正資守備，以靖翰籓，垣壘弗完，營屯未固。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his labor and granted an edict of commendation, saying: "The bulwark of the dry frontier, the choke point of the border—proper reliance on defense to pacify the northern marches. The ramparts were incomplete and the camps not secure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his labor and granted a commendation edict: "The bulwark of the dry frontier, the choke point of the border—proper reliance on defense to pacify the northern marches. The ramparts were incomplete and the camps not secure.

sentences.zh: 卿督茲事役，唯用戍兵，民不知勞，時非淹久，已臻休畢，仍底工堅。

translations.literal: You supervised this work using only garrison troops, so the people knew no toil; the time was not long, yet completion was already achieved, and the work stands firm.
translations.idiomatic: You supervised this work using only garrison troops, so the people knew no toil; the time was not long, yet completion was achieved and the work stands firm.

sentences.zh: 賴爾忠勤，辦茲心畫，有嘉乃力，式副予懷。」

translations.literal: Relying on your loyal diligence in carrying out this plan, your effort is commendable and accords with my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Relying on your loyal diligence in carrying out this plan, your effort is commendable and accords with my intent."

sentences.zh: 賜銀五百兩、重幣十端。

translations.literal: He was granted five hundred taels of silver and ten bolts of heavy brocade.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted five hundred taels of silver and ten bolts of heavy brocade.

sentences.zh: 入為簽樞密院事，轉吏部尚書，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Signing Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was transferred to Minister of Personnel, and appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Signing Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was transferred to Minister of Personnel, and appointed Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 泰和五年，宋渝盟有端，平章政事僕散揆宣撫河南。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe, when Song broke the treaty and gave cause for war, Grand Councilor Pusan Kui was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 5, when Song broke the treaty and gave cause for war, Grand Councilor Pusan Kui was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 揆奏宋人懦弱，韓侂胄用事，請遣使詰問。

translations.literal: Kui memorialized that the Song were weak and that Han Tuozhou held power, requesting that envoys be sent to interrogate them.
translations.idiomatic: Kui memorialized that the Song were weak and Han Tuozhou held power, asking that envoys be sent to interrogate them.

sentences.zh: 上召大臣議。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the chief ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the chief ministers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 左丞相宗浩曰：「宋久敗之國，必不敢動。」

translations.literal: Left Chief Councilor Zong Hao said: "Song is a state long defeated; it will certainly not dare act."
translations.idiomatic: Left Chief Councilor Zong Hao said: "Song is a state long defeated; it will certainly not dare act."

sentences.zh: 思忠曰：「宋雖羈棲江表，未嘗一日忘中國，但力不足耳。」

translations.literal: Sizhong said: "Though Song clings to lands south of the Yangzi, it has never for a single day forgotten the Central Lands—only its strength is insufficient."
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong said: "Though Song clings to lands south of the Yangzi, it has never for a day forgotten the Central Lands—only its strength is insufficient."

sentences.zh: 其後果如思忠策。

translations.literal: Afterward events proved exactly as Sizhong had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward events proved exactly as Sizhong had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，上召大臣議伐宋事，大臣猶言無足慮者。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year the emperor summoned the chief ministers to deliberate on attacking Song; the ministers still said there was nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixth year the emperor summoned the chief ministers to deliberate on attacking Song; the ministers still said there was nothing to worry about.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「鼠竊狗盜，非用兵也。」

translations.literal: Some said: "Rats stealing and dogs snatching—this is not a matter for deploying armies."
translations.idiomatic: Some said: "Rats stealing and dogs snatching—this is not a matter for deploying armies."

sentences.zh: 思忠執前議曰：「不早為之所，彼將誤也。」

translations.literal: Sizhong held to his earlier view, saying: "If we do not act against them early, they will be emboldened."
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong held to his earlier view: "If we do not act against them early, they will be emboldened."

sentences.zh: 上深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply approved this.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，元帥左監軍紇石烈執中圍楚州，久不能下，宰臣奏請命大臣節制其軍，及益兵攻之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, Left Overseer Army Commander Heshilie Zhizhong of the Marshal's staff besieged Chuzhou and could not take it for a long time. The chief ministers memorialized requesting that a chief minister be appointed to command the army and that reinforcements be added for the assault.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year Left Overseer Army Commander Heshilie Zhizhong of the Marshal's staff besieged Chuzhou and could not take it for a long time. The chief ministers memorialized asking that a chief minister command the army and that reinforcements be added.

sentences.zh: 思忠請行。

translations.literal: Sizhong requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong requested to go.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「以執政將兵攻一小州，克之亦不武。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "To send a chief minister as general to attack one small prefecture—even if it is taken, there is nothing martial in it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "To send a chief minister as general to attack one small prefecture—even if taken, there is nothing martial in it."

sentences.zh: 乃用唐宰相宣慰諸軍故事，以思忠充淮南宣慰使，持空名宣敕賞立功者。

translations.literal: He therefore followed the Tang precedent of a chief minister comforting the armies and appointed Sizhong Pacification Commissioner of Huainan, with blank commissions to reward those who achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore followed the Tang precedent of a chief minister comforting the armies and appointed Sizhong Pacification Commissioner of Huainan, with blank commissions to reward merit.

sentences.zh: 詔大臣宿于秘書監，各具奏帖以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the chief ministers to lodge at the Palace Library and each submit a memorial slip for the emperor's review.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the chief ministers to lodge at the Palace Library and each submit a memorial slip for review.

sentences.zh: 明日，詔百官集議於廣仁殿，問對者久之。

translations.literal: The next day an edict ordered all officials to assemble for deliberation in Guangren Hall; question and answer continued for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict ordered all officials to assemble for deliberation in Guangren Hall; question and answer continued for a long time.

sentences.zh: 既而宋人來請和，議遂寢。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Song came to sue for peace, and the plan was set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Song came to sue for peace, and the plan was set aside.

sentences.zh: 頃之，進拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was advanced to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was advanced to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大安初，拜平章政事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Da'an he was appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Da'an he was appointed Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 三年，與參知政事承裕將兵屯邊，方繕完烏沙堡，思忠等不設備，大元前兵奄至，取烏月營，思忠不能守，乃退兵，思忠坐解職。

translations.literal: In the third year, together with Vice Grand Councilor Cheng Yu, he led troops to garrison the frontier and was repairing Wusha Fort when Sizhong and the others made no preparations; the Great Yuan vanguard suddenly arrived and took Wuyue Camp. Sizhong could not hold and withdrew; Sizhong was removed from office for this.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, together with Vice Grand Councilor Cheng Yu, he led troops to garrison the frontier and was repairing Wusha Fort when Sizhong and the others made no preparations; the Great Yuan vanguard suddenly arrived and took Wuyue Camp. Sizhong could not hold and withdrew; he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 衛紹王命參知政事承裕行省，既而敗績於會河堡雲。

translations.literal: Prince Shao of Wei ordered Vice Grand Councilor Cheng Yu to serve as Regional Inspector, and afterward he suffered defeat at Huihe Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shao of Wei ordered Vice Grand Councilor Cheng Yu to serve as Regional Inspector, and afterward he suffered defeat at Huihe Fort.

sentences.zh: 承裕，本名胡沙，頗讀孫、吳書，以宗室子充符寶祗候。

translations.literal: Cheng Yu, original name Husha, read Sunzi and Wuzi extensively and, as a member of the imperial clan, served as Attendant of the Seals and Precious Objects.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yu, birth name Husha, read Sunzi and Wuzi extensively and, as a member of the imperial clan, served as Attendant of the Seals and Precious Objects.

sentences.zh: 除中都左警巡副使，通括戶籍，百姓稱其平。

translations.literal: He was appointed Deputy Commissioner of the Left Metropolitan Patrol of Zhongdu and conducted a census of household registers; the people praised his fairness.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Deputy Commissioner of the Left Metropolitan Patrol of Zhongdu and conducted a census of household registers; the people praised his fairness.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中侍御史，改右警巡使、彰德軍節度副使、刑部員外郎，轉本部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant Censor, then Right Metropolitan Patrol Commissioner, Deputy Military Commissioner of Zhangde Circuit, Outer Office Attendant of the Ministry of Punishments, and then Director of that ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Palace Attendant Censor, then Right Metropolitan Patrol Commissioner, Deputy Military Commissioner of Zhangde Circuit, Outer Office Attendant of the Ministry of Punishments, and then Director of that ministry.

sentences.zh: 曆會州、惠州刺史、遷同知臨潢府事，改東北路招討副使。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Prefect of Huizhou and Huizhou, was promoted to Associate Administrator of Linhuang Prefecture, and was changed to Deputy Pacification Commissioner of the Northeast Route.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Prefect of Huizhou and Huizhou, was promoted to Associate Administrator of Linhuang Prefecture, and was changed to Deputy Pacification Commissioner of the Northeast Route.

sentences.zh: 以病免，起為西南招討副使。

translations.literal: He was dismissed on grounds of illness, then recalled as Deputy Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Route.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed on grounds of illness, then recalled as Deputy Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Route.

sentences.zh: 泰和六年，伐宋，遷陝西路統軍副使，俄改通遠軍節度使、陝西兵馬都統副使，與秦州防禦使完顏璘屯成紀界。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe, when Song was attacked, he was promoted to Deputy Commander of the Shaanxi Circuit Army; soon he was changed to Military Commissioner of Tongyuan Army and Deputy Commander-in-chief of Shaanxi forces, and with Qinzhou Defense Commissioner Wanyan Lin he garrisoned the Chengji frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 6, during the attack on Song, he was promoted to Deputy Commander of the Shaanxi Circuit Army; soon he was changed to Military Commissioner of Tongyuan Army and Deputy Commander-in-chief of Shaanxi forces, and with Qinzhou Defense Commissioner Wanyan Lin he garrisoned the Chengji frontier.

sentences.zh: 宋吳曦兵五萬由保岔、姑蘇等谷襲秦州，承裕、璘以騎兵千餘人擊走之，追奔四十里，凡六戰，宋兵大敗，斬首四千餘級。

translations.literal: Song Wu Xi's army of fifty thousand came through Baicha, Gusu, and other passes to raid Qinzhou; Cheng Yu and Lin with more than a thousand horsemen drove them off and pursued forty li. In six battles the Song army was utterly defeated, with more than four thousand heads taken.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi of Song led fifty thousand men through Baicha, Gusu, and other passes to raid Qinzhou; Cheng Yu and Lin with more than a thousand horsemen drove them off and pursued forty li. In six battles the Song army was utterly defeated and more than four thousand heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 詔承裕曰：「昔乃祖乃父，戮力戎旅，汝年尚少，善於其職，故命汝與完顏璘同行出界。

translations.literal: An edict to Cheng Yu said: "In former times your ancestors and father exerted themselves in military service. You are still young and skilled in your duties; therefore I appoint you to go beyond the frontier with Wanyan Lin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to Cheng Yu said: "Your ancestors and father once exerted themselves in military service. You are still young and skilled in your duties; therefore I appoint you to go beyond the frontier with Wanyan Lin.

sentences.zh: 昔汝自言得兵三萬足以辦事，今以石抹仲溫、術虎高琪及青宜可與汝軍相合，計可六萬，斯亦足以辦矣。

translations.literal: You once said yourself that thirty thousand troops would be enough to accomplish the task. Now with Shi Mo Zhongwen, Tuhu Gaoqi, and Qing Yi Ke joining your army, the total should reach sixty thousand—that too is enough to accomplish it.
translations.idiomatic: You once said yourself that thirty thousand troops would be enough. Now with Shi Mo Zhongwen, Tuhu Gaoqi, and Qing Yi Ke joining your army, the total should reach sixty thousand—that too should be enough.

sentences.zh: 仲溫、高琪兵道險阻，汝兵道甚易也。

translations.literal: Zhongwen's and Gaoqi's routes are rugged, while yours is very easy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen's and Gaoqi's routes are rugged, while yours is very easy.

sentences.zh: 自秦州至仙人關才四百里耳，從長計畫，以副朕意。」

translations.literal: From Qinzhou to Xianren Pass is only four hundred li. Plan for the long term and accord with my intent."
translations.idiomatic: From Qinzhou to Xianren Pass is only four hundred li. Plan for the long term and accord with my intent."

sentences.zh: 詔完顏璘曰：「汝向在北邊，以幹勇見稱，頃以過失，逮問有司。

translations.literal: An edict to Wanyan Lin said: "You were once known on the northern frontier for dry courage; recently, because of an offense, you were brought before the authorities for inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to Wanyan Lin said: "You were once known on the northern frontier for dry courage; recently, because of an offense, you were brought before the authorities.

sentences.zh: 近知與宋人奮戰，故特赦免，仍充副統，如能佐承裕立功業，朕於官賞，豈複吝惜。

translations.literal: Learning that you fought fiercely against the Song, I therefore specially pardoned you and again made you deputy commander-in-chief. If you can assist Cheng Yu in achieving merit, in official rewards and favors I shall certainly not be sparing.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that you fought fiercely against the Song, I therefore specially pardoned you and again made you deputy commander-in-chief. If you can assist Cheng Yu in achieving merit, in rewards and favors I shall certainly not be sparing.

sentences.zh: 聞汝臨事頗黠，若複自速罪，且不赦汝矣。」

translations.literal: I hear that in action you are rather cunning; if you again hasten into guilt yourself, I shall not pardon you."
translations.idiomatic: I hear that in action you are rather cunning; if you again hasten into guilt, I shall not pardon you."

sentences.zh: 宋吳曦使其將馮興、楊雄、李珪以步騎八千入赤穀，承裕、璘及河州防禦使蒲察秉鉉逆擊破之。

translations.literal: Song Wu Xi sent his generals Feng Xing, Yang Xiong, and Li Gui with eight thousand infantry and cavalry into Chigu; Cheng Yu, Lin, and Hezhou Defense Commissioner Pucha Bingxuan met and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi of Song sent his generals Feng Xing, Yang Xiong, and Li Gui with eight thousand infantry and cavalry into Chigu; Cheng Yu, Lin, and Hezhou Defense Commissioner Pucha Bingxuan met and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 宋步兵保西山，騎兵走赤穀。

translations.literal: The Song infantry held West Mountain; the cavalry fled to Chigu.
translations.idiomatic: The Song infantry held West Mountain; the cavalry fled to Chigu.

sentences.zh: 承裕遣部將唐括按答海率騎二百馳擊宋步兵，甲士蒙括挺身先入乘之，宋步兵大潰。

translations.literal: Cheng Yu sent his subordinate Tangut Anda Hai with two hundred horsemen to charge the Song infantry; armored soldier Meng Kuo thrust himself forward first and broke them; the Song infantry was utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yu sent his subordinate Tangut Anda Hai with two hundred horsemen to charge the Song infantry; armored soldier Meng Kuo thrust himself forward first and broke them, and the Song infantry was utterly routed.

sentences.zh: 追奔至皁郊城，斬二千餘級。

translations.literal: The pursuit ran to Zaoqiao city, with more than two thousand heads taken.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit ran to Zaoqiao city, with more than two thousand heads taken.

sentences.zh: 猛安把添奴追宋騎兵，殺千餘人，斬楊雄、李珪于陣，馮興僅以身免。

translations.literal: Meng'an Batiannu pursued the Song cavalry, killing more than a thousand men and slaying Yang Xiong and Li Gui in battle; Feng Xing barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Meng'an Batiannu pursued the Song cavalry, killing more than a thousand men and slaying Yang Xiong and Li Gui in battle; Feng Xing barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 承裕進兵，克成州。

translations.literal: Cheng Yu advanced his army and took Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yu advanced his army and took Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，罷兵，遷河南東路統軍使，兼知歸德府事，俄改知臨潢府事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the armies were disbanded; he was transferred to Commander of the Eastern Henan Route Army and Concurrent Administrator of Guide Prefecture, soon changed to Administrator of Linhuang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the armies were disbanded; he was transferred to Commander of the Eastern Henan Route Army and concurrent Administrator of Guide Prefecture, soon changed to Administrator of Linhuang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 賜金帶、重幣十端、銀百五十兩。

translations.literal: He was granted a gold belt, ten bolts of heavy brocade, and one hundred fifty taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a gold belt, ten bolts of heavy brocade, and one hundred fifty taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 大安初，召為禦史中丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Da'an he was summoned as Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Da'an he was summoned as Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜參知政事，與平章政事獨吉思忠行省戍邊。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor and, together with Grand Councilor Duji Sizhong, served as Regional Inspector garrisoning the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor and, together with Grand Councilor Duji Sizhong, served as Regional Inspector garrisoning the frontier.

sentences.zh: 烏沙堡之役，不為備，失利，朝廷獨坐思忠，詔承裕主兵事。

translations.literal: In the battle of Wusha Fort they made no preparations and suffered defeat; the court held only Sizhong responsible and ordered Cheng Yu to take charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At Wusha Fort they made no preparations and suffered defeat; the court held only Sizhong responsible and ordered Cheng Yu to take charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：曹劌有言：「一鼓作氣，再而衰，三而竭。」

translations.literal: The commentator says: Cao Gui had a saying: "At the first drum, courage is roused; at the second it fades; at the third it is exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Cao Gui said, "At the first drum courage is roused; at the second it fades; at the third it is exhausted."

sentences.zh: 夫兵以氣為主，會河堡之役，獨吉思忠、承裕沮喪不可複振，金之亡國，兆於此焉。

translations.literal: War depends on spirit; at the battle of Huihe Fort, Duji Sizhong and Cheng Yu were so crushed that they could not be rallied again—the destruction of Jin was foreshadowed here.
translations.idiomatic: War depends on spirit; at Huihe Fort Duji Sizhong and Cheng Yu were so crushed they could not be rallied again—the destruction of Jin was foreshadowed here.

sentences.zh: 僕散揆

translations.literal: Pusan Kui
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Kui

sentences.zh: 僕散揆，本名臨喜，其先上京人，左丞相兼都元帥沂國武莊公忠義之子也。

translations.literal: Pusan Kui, original name Linxi, was a native of Shangjing; he was the son of Left Chief Councilor and Concurrent Commander-in-chief Duke Wu of Yi, Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Kui, birth name Linxi, was a native of Shangjing; he was son of Left Chief Councilor and Concurrent Commander-in-chief Duke Wu of Yi, Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 少以世胄，選為近侍奉禦。

translations.literal: In youth, by virtue of his noble lineage, he was selected as a close attendant serving the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In youth, by virtue of his noble lineage, he was selected as a close attendant serving the emperor.

sentences.zh: 大定十五年，尚韓國大長公主，擢器物局副使，特授臨潢府路赫沙阿世襲猛安。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Dading he married the Grand Princess of Han and was promoted to Deputy Commissioner of the Implements Bureau; he was specially granted the hereditary meng'an of Hesha in Linhuang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 15 he married the Grand Princess of Han and was promoted to Deputy Commissioner of the Implements Bureau; he was specially granted the hereditary meng'an of Hesha in Linhuang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 曆近侍局副使、尚衣局使、拱衛直副都指揮使，為殿前左衛將軍。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Deputy Commissioner of the Close Attendants Bureau, Commissioner of the Imperial Wardrobe Bureau, Deputy Commander of the Imperial Guard Direct, and Left Guard General of the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Deputy Commissioner of the Close Attendants Bureau, Commissioner of the Imperial Wardrobe Bureau, Deputy Commander of the Imperial Guard Direct, and Left Guard General of the Palace Front.

sentences.zh: 罷職，世宗諭之曰：「以汝宣獻皇后之親，故令尚主，置之宿衛，謂當以忠孝自勵。

translations.literal: He was dismissed from office. Shizong admonished him: "Because you are kin to Empress Xuanxian, I had you marry a princess and placed you in the palace guard, thinking you would encourage yourself with loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed. Shizong admonished him: "Because you are kin to Empress Xuanxian, I had you marry a princess and placed you in the palace guard, thinking you would encourage yourself with loyalty and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 日者乃與外人竊議，汝腹中事，朕不能測，其罷歸田里。」

translations.literal: Yet lately you have discussed matters in secret with outsiders. The affairs in your belly I cannot fathom—return to your home village."
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately you have discussed matters in secret with outsiders. What is in your belly I cannot fathom—return to your home village."

sentences.zh: 尋起為濼州刺史，改蠡州，入為兵部侍郎、大理卿、刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as Prefect of Liao Prefecture, changed to Li Prefecture, and entered the capital as Vice Minister of War, Grand Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, and Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as Prefect of Liao Prefecture, changed to Li Prefecture, and entered the capital as Vice Minister of War, Grand Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, and Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，出為泰定軍節度使，改知臨洮府事。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong took the throne, he went out as Military Commissioner of Taiding Army and was changed to Administrator of Lintao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong acceded, he went out as Military Commissioner of Taiding Army and was changed to Administrator of Lintao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以政績聞。

translations.literal: He became known for his administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He became known for his administrative achievements.

sentences.zh: 升河南路統軍使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commander of the Henan Route Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commander of the Henan Route Army.

sentences.zh: 陝西提刑司舉揆「剛直明斷，獄無冤滯。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi Judicial Commission recommended Kui as "upright, clear, and decisive, with no wrongful delays in cases.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi Judicial Commission recommended Kui as "upright, clear, and decisive, with no wrongful delays in cases.

sentences.zh: 禁戢家人，百姓莫識其面。

translations.literal: He restrained his household; the common people did not even know his face.
translations.idiomatic: He restrained his household; the common people did not even know his face.

sentences.zh: 積石、洮二州舊寇皆遁，商旅得通」。

translations.literal: The old bandits of Jishi and Tao prefectures all fled; merchants could travel freely."
translations.idiomatic: The old bandits of Jishi and Tao prefectures all fled away, and merchants could pass freely."

sentences.zh: 於是進官一階，仍詔褒諭。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was promoted one rank in office, and an edict commending him was also issued.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was promoted one rank, and the court also issued an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 明昌四年，鄭王永蹈謀逆，事覺，揆坐嘗私品藻諸王，獨稱永蹈性善，靜不好事，乃免死，除名。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Mingchang, the Prince of Zheng, Yong Tao, plotted rebellion; when the affair was discovered, Kui was implicated because he had privately appraised the princes and alone praised Yong Tao as good-natured, quiet, and averse to trouble — and so was spared death but stripped of his name and office.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 4, the Prince of Zheng, Yong Tao, plotted rebellion. When the plot was exposed, Kui was implicated for having privately appraised the princes and singling out Yong Tao as good-natured, quiet, and unambitious. He was spared death but dismissed and stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 未幾，複五品階，起為同知崇義軍節度使事。

translations.literal: Before long, his fifth-rank status was restored, and he was recalled as Vice Commissioner of the Chongyi Army Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his fifth-rank status was restored, and he was recalled as deputy commissioner of the Chongyi Army.

sentences.zh: 以戰功遷西北路副招討，進官七階，賜金馬盂一、銀二百兩、重彩一十端。

translations.literal: For military merit he was transferred to Deputy Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Route, promoted seven ranks in office, and granted one gold horse-cup, two hundred taels of silver, and ten bolts of fine silk.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit he was made Deputy Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Route, promoted seven ranks, and granted a gold horse-cup, two hundred taels of silver, and ten bolts of fine silk.

sentences.zh: 複以戰功升西南路招討使兼天德軍節度使，賜金五十兩、重彩一十端。

translations.literal: Again for military merit he was promoted to Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Route and concurrently Military Commissioner of the Tiande Army, and was granted fifty taels of gold and ten bolts of fine silk.
translations.idiomatic: Again for military merit he was promoted to Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Route and concurrent Military Commissioner of the Tiande Army, with fifty taels of gold and ten bolts of fine silk.

sentences.zh: 複出禦邊，當轉戰出塞七百里，至赤胡睹地而還。

translations.literal: Again he went out to defend the frontier; in the course of fighting he crossed the border seven hundred li, reaching Chihududi before returning.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to defend the frontier again and, fighting as he went, crossed the border seven hundred li, reaching Chihududi before turning back.

sentences.zh: 優詔褒諭，遷一官，仍許其子安貞尚邢國長公主，且許揆入謝，禮成，歸鎮。

translations.literal: An exceptional edict commended him; he was transferred one rank in office, and his son Anzhen was permitted to marry the Princess Chang of Xing State. Kui was also allowed to enter court to give thanks; when the rites were complete, he returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a special commendation and promoted him one rank. His son Anzhen was permitted to marry the Princess Chang of Xing State, and Kui was allowed to enter court to give thanks. When the ceremony was complete, he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 會韓國大長公主薨，揆來赴，上諭之曰：「北邊之事，非卿不能辦。」

translations.literal: When the Grand Princess of Han State died, Kui came to attend the mourning. The emperor instructed him, saying: "Affairs on the northern frontier cannot be managed without you."
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Princess of Han State died, Kui came to attend the mourning. The emperor told him: "Affairs on the northern frontier cannot be managed without you."

sentences.zh: 乃賜戰馬二，即日遣還。

translations.literal: He then granted two war-horses and sent him back the same day.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted him two war-horses and sent him back the same day.

sentences.zh: 揆沿徼築壘穿塹，連亙九百里，營柵相望，烽候相應，人得恣田牧，北邊遂寧。

translations.literal: Kui built fortresses and dug moats along the frontier, stretching unbroken for nine hundred li; camps and palisades faced one another, beacon towers answered one another, and the people were able to pasture and farm at will — and the northern frontier was thereafter at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Kui built fortresses and dug moats along the frontier for nine hundred li without a break. Camps and palisades stood face to face, beacon towers answered one another, and the people could pasture and farm freely; the northern frontier was finally at peace.

sentences.zh: 複以手詔褒諭，且欲大用，以知興中府事紇石烈子仁代之，敕盡以方略授子仁。

translations.literal: Again he was commended by handwritten edict, and the emperor wished to employ him on a grand scale; Ziren of the Heshenlie clan, Administrator of Xingzhong Prefecture, was appointed in his place, and an order was issued to impart to Ziren the full strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He was commended again by handwritten edict, and the emperor intended to give him greater employment. Ziren of the Heshenlie clan, who governed Xingzhong Prefecture, replaced him, and Kui was ordered to pass on his full strategy.

sentences.zh: 既入，拜參知政事，改授中都路胡土愛割蠻世襲猛安。

translations.literal: Once he had entered the capital, he was appointed Associate Administrator of Affairs and was reassigned the hereditary meng'an of Hutuai Geman on the Zhongdu Route.
translations.idiomatic: On entering the capital he was appointed Associate Administrator of Affairs and reassigned the hereditary meng'an of Hutuai Geman on the Zhongdu Route.

sentences.zh: 進拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋出經略邊事，還拜平章政事，封濟國公。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he went out to oversee frontier affairs; on his return he was appointed Grand Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Ji State.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he went out to oversee frontier affairs. On his return he was appointed Grand Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Ji State.

sentences.zh: 六年春，宋人複數路來侵，取泗州，取靈璧，圍壽春。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year, the Song again invaded by several routes, taking Sizhou and Lingbi and besieging Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year, the Song invaded again on several routes, taking Sizhou and Lingbi and besieging Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 命揆為左副元帥以討之。

translations.literal: Kui was appointed Left Deputy Commander-in-chief to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was appointed Left Deputy Commander-in-chief to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 揆至軍前，集諸將校告以朝廷吊伐之意，分遣將士禦敵。

translations.literal: When Kui reached the army, he assembled the generals and officers and declared the court's intent to succor the wronged and punish the guilty, then dispatched officers and soldiers to resist the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Kui reached the army, he assembled the generals and officers, declared the court's intent to succor the wronged and punish the guilty, and dispatched troops to resist the enemy.

sentences.zh: 複取臨淮、蘄縣，而符離、壽春之圍亦解去，敵屢敗衄，悉遁出境。

translations.literal: He recovered Linhuai and Qixian, and the sieges of Fuli and Shouchun were also lifted; the enemy suffered repeated defeats and all fled beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Linhuai and Qixian, lifted the sieges of Fuli and Shouchun, and drove the enemy, repeatedly defeated, back across the border.

sentences.zh: 上即遣提點近侍局烏古論慶壽持手詔勞問征討事宜，仍賜玉具劍一、玉荷蓮盞一、金器一百兩、重彩一十端。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately dispatched Wugulun Qingshou of the Palace Attendants Bureau, bearing a handwritten edict to inquire after the campaign and commend him, and also granted one jade-fitted sword, one jade lotus goblet, one hundred taels of gold vessels, and ten bolts of fine silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately sent Wugulun Qingshou of the Palace Attendants Bureau with a handwritten edict to inquire after the campaign and commend him, granting a jade-fitted sword, a jade lotus goblet, one hundred taels of gold vessels, and ten bolts of fine silk.

sentences.zh: 尋複以詔褒諭，賜玉鞍勒馬二及玉具佩刀、內府重彩、禦藥，以旌其功。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was again commended by edict and granted two horses with jade saddles and bridles, a jade-fitted girdle knife, fine silk from the inner treasury, and imperial medicine, to honor his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was commended again by edict and granted two horses with jade saddles and bridles, a jade-fitted girdle knife, fine silk from the inner treasury, and imperial medicine in recognition of his merit.

sentences.zh: 宋人既敗退，上欲進討，乃召揆赴闕，戒以師期，宴于慶和殿，親諭之曰：「朕以趙擴背盟，侵我疆埸，命卿措畫。

translations.literal: After the Song had been defeated and withdrawn, the emperor wished to advance in pursuit and summoned Kui to court, setting a date for the army's departure. He feasted him in the Hall of Celebratory Harmony and personally instructed him, saying: "Because Zhao Kuo broke the treaty and invaded our borders, I ordered you to plan the response.
translations.idiomatic: After the Song had been beaten back, the emperor wished to advance in pursuit and summoned Kui to court, fixing a date for the army's departure. He feasted him in the Hall of Celebratory Harmony and told him personally: "Because Zhao Kuo broke the treaty and invaded our borders, I ordered you to plan the response.

sentences.zh: 曾未期月，諸處累報大捷。

translations.literal: In less than a full month, repeated reports of great victories arrived from every quarter.
translations.idiomatic: In less than a month, great victories were reported from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 振我國威，挫彼賊鋒，皆卿之力，朕不能忘。」

translations.literal: To revive our nation's prestige and blunt the enemy's edge — all this is your doing, and I cannot forget it."
translations.idiomatic: You have revived our nation's prestige and blunted the enemy's edge — all of it is your doing, and I shall not forget it."

sentences.zh: 是日寵錫甚厚，特收其次子甯壽為奉禦，乃密授以成算，俾還軍。

translations.literal: That day he was favored with lavish gifts; his second son Ningshou was specially enrolled as a Palace Attendant. The emperor then secretly entrusted him with the completed plan and sent him back to the army.
translations.idiomatic: That day he received lavish gifts, and his second son Ningshou was specially enrolled as a Palace Attendant. The emperor then secretly entrusted him with the completed plan and sent him back to the army.

sentences.zh: 十月，揆總大軍南伐，分兵為九路進。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Kui commanded the great army in a southern campaign, dividing the forces to advance by nine routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Kui commanded the great army southward, dividing his forces to advance along nine routes.

sentences.zh: 揆以行省兵三萬出潁、壽，至淮，宋人旅拒于水南。

translations.literal: Kui led thirty thousand provincial troops out from Ying and Shou, reached the Huai River, and found the Song arrayed in defense on the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: Kui led thirty thousand provincial troops out from Ying and Shou. When he reached the Huai, the Song had massed in defense on the south bank.

sentences.zh: 揆密遣人測淮水，惟八疊灘可涉，即遣奧屯驤揚兵下蔡，聲言欲渡。

translations.literal: Kui secretly sent men to sound the Huai; only at Badie Ford could it be forded. He then dispatched Aotun Xiang to display troops at Xia Cai, proclaiming an intent to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Kui secretly sent men to sound the Huai and found that only Badie Ford was fordable. He then sent Aotun Xiang to display troops at Xia Cai, proclaiming that he intended to cross there.

sentences.zh: 宋帥何汝礪、姚公佐悉銳師屯花靨以備。
