translations.literal: The Song commanders He Ruli and Yao Gongzuo massed their elite forces at Huayan to guard against it.
translations.idiomatic: The Song commanders He Ruli and Yao Gongzuo massed their elite forces at Huayan to guard against it.

sentences.zh: 揆乃遣右翼都統完顏賽不、先鋒都統納蘭邦烈潛渡八疊，駐南岸。

translations.literal: Kui then sent the Right Wing Commander-in-chief Wanyan Saibu and Vanguard Commander-in-chief Nalan Bangle to cross secretly at Badie and encamp on the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: Kui then sent Right Wing Commander-in-chief Wanyan Saibu and Vanguard Commander-in-chief Nalan Bangle to ford Badie in secret and encamp on the south bank.

sentences.zh: 揆麾大軍直壓其陣。

translations.literal: Kui led the great army straight against their formation.
translations.idiomatic: Kui then led the main army straight against their formation.

sentences.zh: 敵不虞我卒至，皆潰走，自相蹂踐，死于水者不可勝計。

translations.literal: The enemy did not expect our sudden arrival; all broke and fled, trampling one another, and those who died in the water were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy did not expect so sudden an arrival. They broke and fled, trampling one another, and those who drowned were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 進奪潁口，下安豐軍，遂攻合肥，取滁州，盡獲其軍實。

translations.literal: Advancing, he seized Yingkou, took Anfeng Army, then attacked Hefei, captured Chuzhou, and seized all their military stores.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to seize Yingkou, took Anfeng Army, then attacked Hefei, captured Chuzhou, and seized all their military stores.

sentences.zh: 上遣使諭之曰：「前得卿奏，先鋒已奪潁口，偏師又下安豐，斬馘之數，各以萬計。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy to instruct him, saying: "In your earlier memorial, the vanguard had already taken Yingkou and a detached force had also taken Anfeng; the numbers of heads taken and enemies slain were each in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to instruct him, saying: "Your earlier memorial reported that the vanguard had already taken Yingkou and a detached force had also taken Anfeng; heads taken and enemies slain were each counted in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 近又西帥奏捷，棗陽、光化既為我有，樊城、鄧城亦自潰散。

translations.literal: Recently the western commander also reported victory: Zaoyang and Guanghua are already ours, and Fancheng and Dengcheng have also collapsed on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the western commander also reported victory: Zaoyang and Guanghua are already ours, and Fancheng and Dengcheng have collapsed on their own.

sentences.zh: 又聞隨州闔城歸順，山東之眾久圍楚州，隴右之師克期出界。

translations.literal: I have also heard that Suizhou has submitted as a whole city; the eastern forces have long besieged Chuzhou, and the Longyou army is set to cross the border on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that Suizhou has submitted entire; eastern forces have long besieged Chuzhou, and the Longyou army is set to cross the border on schedule.

sentences.zh: 卿提大兵攻合肥，趙擴聞之，料已破膽，失其神守。

translations.literal: You lead the great army against Hefei; when Zhao Kuo hears of it, I expect he will already be terrified and lose his composure.
translations.idiomatic: You are leading the great army against Hefei. When Zhao Kuo hears of it, I expect he will be terrified out of his wits.

sentences.zh: 度彼之計，乞和為上，昔嘗畫三事付卿，以今事勢計之，徑渡長江，亦其時矣。

translations.literal: Judging their plan, suing for peace would be their best course. I once set forth three matters for you; given the present situation, crossing the Yangtze directly is also timely.
translations.idiomatic: Judging their plan, suing for peace would be their best course. I once entrusted you with three objectives; given the present situation, crossing the Yangtze directly is also timely.

sentences.zh: 淮南既為我有，際江為界，理所宜然。

translations.literal: Since Huainan is already ours, taking the river as the border is as reason demands.
translations.idiomatic: Since Huainan is already ours, making the river the border is only reasonable.

sentences.zh: 如使趙擴奉表稱臣，歲增貢幣，縛送賊魁，還所俘掠，一如所諭，亦可罷兵。

translations.literal: If Zhao Kuo submits a memorial calling himself a subject, increases the annual tribute, binds and sends the rebel leaders, and returns those captured and plundered — all as instructed — we may also cease hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: If Zhao Kuo submits a memorial calling himself our subject, increases the annual tribute, binds and sends the rebel leaders, and returns those captured and plundered — all as instructed — we may also cease hostilities.

sentences.zh: 卿宜廣為渡江之勢，使彼有必死之憂，從其所請而縱之，僅得餘息偷生，豈敢複萌他慮。

translations.literal: You should broadly create the appearance of crossing the river, so that they feel the dread of certain death; grant their request and release them, and they will barely have breath left to live on — how would they dare again harbor other designs?
translations.idiomatic: You should broadly create the appearance of crossing the river so that they feel the dread of certain death. Grant their request and release them, and they will barely have breath left to live on — how would they dare harbor other designs?

sentences.zh: 卿於此時，經營江北，勞徠安集，除其虐政橫賦，以良吏撫字疲民，以精兵分守要害，雖未系趙擴之頸，而朕前所畫三事，上功已成矣。

translations.literal: At this time, manage the north of the river: labor to win men over, settle and gather them, remove cruel government and oppressive levies, place good officials to nurture the weary people, and station elite troops to guard key points. Even if you have not yet put a rope around Zhao Kuo's neck, the upper of the three matters I earlier planned will already be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, manage the north of the river: win men over with labor and care, settle and gather them, remove cruel government and oppressive levies, place good officials to nurture the weary people, and station elite troops at key points. Even if you have not yet put a rope around Zhao Kuo's neck, the foremost of the three objectives I planned will already be accomplished.

sentences.zh: 前入見時，已嘗議定，今複諄諄者，欲決卿成功爾。

translations.literal: When you last came to audience, this was already settled; the reason I repeat myself so earnestly now is that I wish to see you succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When you last came to audience, this was already settled. I repeat myself so earnestly now because I want to see you succeed.

sentences.zh: 機會難遇，卿其勉之。」

translations.literal: Opportunity is hard to meet — exert yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Opportunity is hard to come by — exert yourself."

sentences.zh: 既而宋帥丘灊果奉書乞和，揆以前五事諭而遣之。

translations.literal: Before long the Song commander Qiu Kan indeed sent a letter begging for peace; Kui set forth the five prior conditions, instructed him, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Song commander Qiu Kan sent a letter begging for peace. Kui set forth the five prior conditions, instructed him, and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 複進軍圍和州，敵以騎萬五千駐六合，揆偵知之，即以右翼掩擊，斬首八千級，進屯于瓦梁河，以控真、揚諸路之沖。

translations.literal: Again he advanced and besieged Hezhou; the enemy stationed fifteen thousand cavalry at Luhe. Kui learned of it by reconnaissance and immediately sent the right wing to strike from concealment, taking eight thousand heads. He advanced and encamped at Waliang River to control the crossings of Zhen and Yang routes.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced again and besieged Hezhou. The enemy stationed fifteen thousand cavalry at Luhe; Kui learned of it by reconnaissance and sent the right wing to strike from concealment, taking eight thousand heads. He advanced and encamped at Waliang River to control the crossings of the Zhen and Yang routes.

sentences.zh: 乃整列軍騎，畢張旗幟，沿江上下，皆金兵焉。

translations.literal: He then arrayed cavalry and infantry in order, fully displayed banners and flags, and up and down the riverbank there were Jin troops everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: He then arrayed cavalry and infantry in order, fully displayed banners and flags, and Jin troops lined the river up and down.

sentences.zh: 於是江表震恐。

translations.literal: Thereupon the region south of the river was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: The region south of the river was shaken with terror.

sentences.zh: 宋真州兵數萬保河橋，複遣統軍紇石烈子仁往攻之，分軍涉淺，潛出敵後。

translations.literal: Several tens of thousands of Song troops at Zhenzhou held the river bridge; Kui again dispatched Commander-in-chief Ziren of the Heshenlie clan to attack them, dividing the army to ford the shallows and steal out behind the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Several tens of thousands of Song troops at Zhenzhou held the river bridge. Kui again sent Commander-in-chief Ziren of the Heshenlie clan to attack them, dividing his army to ford the shallows and steal out behind the enemy.

sentences.zh: 敵見之大驚，不戰而潰，斬首二萬餘級，生擒其帥劉侹、常思敬、蕭從德、莫子容，皆宋驍將也。

translations.literal: When the enemy saw this they were greatly alarmed; without fighting they broke and fled. More than twenty thousand heads were taken, and their commanders Liu Ting, Chang Sijing, Xiao Congde, and Mo Zirong were captured alive — all fierce Song generals.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy saw this they were greatly alarmed and broke without fighting. More than twenty thousand heads were taken, and their commanders Liu Ting, Chang Sijing, Xiao Congde, and Mo Zirong were captured alive — all fierce Song generals.

sentences.zh: 遂下真州。

translations.literal: He then took Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋複遣陳璧來告和，揆以乞辭未誠，徒欲緩師，欲之。

translations.literal: The Song again sent Chen Bi to announce peace; Kui held that the language of supplication was not sincere and merely intended to delay the army, and did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The Song again sent Chen Bi to sue for peace. Kui judged the terms insincere and merely a stall for time, and refused them.

sentences.zh: 宋人既喪敗，不獲請成，乃決巨勝、成公、雷塘渚積水以為阻，盡焚其廬舍儲積，過江遁去。

translations.literal: The Song, having suffered defeat, failed to obtain peace; they then breached the dikes at Jusheng, Chenggong, and Leitangzhu to store up water as a barrier, burned all their buildings and stores, and fled across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Having suffered defeat and failed to obtain peace, the Song breached the dikes at Jusheng, Chenggong, and Leitangzhu to store up water as a barrier, burned all their buildings and stores, and fled across the river.

sentences.zh: 揆體剛內和，與物無忤，臨民有惠政。

translations.literal: Kui's body was stern yet inwardly harmonious; he did not clash with others, and in governing the people he had benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was stern in bearing yet inwardly harmonious. He did not clash with others, and in governing the people he carried out benevolent policies.

sentences.zh: 其為將也，軍門鎮靜，嘗罰必行。

translations.literal: As a general, he kept the army gate calm and quiet, and punishments he imposed were always carried out.
translations.idiomatic: As a general he kept the army gate calm and quiet, and punishments he imposed were always enforced.

sentences.zh: 初渡淮，即命徹去浮梁。

translations.literal: As soon as he crossed the Huai, he ordered the floating bridges removed.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he crossed the Huai, he ordered the floating bridges removed.

sentences.zh: 所至皆因糧於敵，無饋運之勞。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he took grain from the enemy, without the labor of supply transport.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went he lived off enemy grain, without the burden of supply lines.

sentences.zh: 未嘗輕用士卒，而與之同甘苦，人亦樂為之用。

translations.literal: He never lightly expended his soldiers, yet shared hardship and comfort with them, and men were also glad to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: He never lightly expended his soldiers, yet shared their hardships and comforts, and his men were glad to serve him.

sentences.zh: 故南征北伐，為一代名將雲。

translations.literal: Thus in southern campaigns and northern expeditions he was a famous general of his generation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in southern campaigns and northern expeditions he was accounted a famous general of his generation.

sentences.zh: 抹撚史乂搭

translations.literal: Monian Shiguda
translations.idiomatic: Monian Shiguda

sentences.zh: 抹撚史乂搭，臨潢路人也。

translations.literal: Monian Shiguda was a man of Linhuang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Monian Shiguda was a native of Linhuang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 其先以功授世襲謀克。

translations.literal: His forebears had been granted a hereditary mouke for merit.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had been granted a hereditary mouke for merit.

sentences.zh: 史乂搭幼襲爵，守邊有勞。

translations.literal: Shiguda inherited the title while young and had merit in guarding the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Shiguda inherited the title while young and earned merit guarding the frontier.

sentences.zh: 泰和六年，南鄙用兵，授同知蔡州防禦使事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe, when troops were deployed on the southern frontier, he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Cai Prefecture Defense Command.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 6, when troops were deployed on the southern frontier, he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Cai Prefecture Defense Command.

sentences.zh: 五月，宋將李爽圍壽州，田俊邁陷蘄縣，平章政事僕散揆謂諸將曰：「符離、彭城，齊魯之蔽，符離不守，是無彭城，彭城陷則齊魯危矣。」

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Song general Li Shuang besieged Shouchun and Tian Junmai took Qixian. Grand Councilor Pusan Kui told the generals: "Fuli and Pengcheng are the shield of Qi and Lu; if Fuli is not held, there is no Pengcheng — and if Pengcheng falls, Qi and Lu are in peril."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the Song general Li Shuang besieged Shouchun and Tian Junmai took Qixian. Grand Councilor Pusan Kui told the generals: "Fuli and Pengcheng are the shield of Qi and Lu. If Fuli is not held, Pengcheng cannot stand — and if Pengcheng falls, Qi and Lu are in peril."

sentences.zh: 乃遣安國軍節度副使納蘭邦烈與史乂搭以精騎三千戍宿州。

translations.literal: He then dispatched Nalan Bangle, Deputy Military Commissioner of the Anguo Army, and Shiguda with three thousand elite cavalry to garrison Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then dispatched Nalan Bangle, Deputy Military Commissioner of the Anguo Army, and Shiguda with three thousand elite cavalry to garrison Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 俊邁果率步騎二萬來襲，邦烈、史乂搭逆擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Junmai indeed led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack; Bangle and Shiguda met them and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Junmai indeed led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack. Bangle and Shiguda met them and routed them.

sentences.zh: 邦烈中流矢。

translations.literal: Bangle was struck by a flying arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Bangle was struck by a flying arrow.

sentences.zh: 宋郭倬、李汝翼以眾五萬繼至，遂圍城，攻之甚力，城中叢射，敵不能逼。

translations.literal: Guo Zhuo and Li Ruyi of Song came afterward with fifty thousand men, then besieged the city and attacked with great force; the city answered with dense volleys, and the enemy could not press close.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhuo and Li Ruyi of Song came afterward with fifty thousand men, besieged the city, and attacked with great force. The defenders answered with dense volleys, and the enemy could not press close.

sentences.zh: 會淫雨潦溢，敵露處勞倦，邦烈遣騎二百潛出敵後突擊之。

translations.literal: When heavy rains flooded the fields, the enemy, exposed and weary, Bangle sent two hundred cavalry to steal out behind them and strike suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: When heavy rains flooded the fields, the exposed and weary enemy was struck by two hundred cavalry Bangle sent to steal out behind them.

sentences.zh: 敵亂，史乂搭率騎蹂之，殺傷數千人。

translations.literal: The enemy fell into disorder; Shiguda led cavalry to trample them, killing and wounding several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fell into disorder. Shiguda led cavalry to trample them, killing and wounding several thousand.

sentences.zh: 敵複聞援軍將至，遂夜遁。

translations.literal: The enemy again heard that relief troops were about to arrive and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy again heard that relief troops were about to arrive and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 邦烈、史乂搭躡其後，黎明合擊，大破之，獲田俊邁。

translations.literal: Bangle and Shiguda pursued them; at dawn they joined in the attack and routed them greatly, capturing Tian Junmai.
translations.idiomatic: Bangle and Shiguda pursued them. At dawn they joined in the attack, routed them completely, and captured Tian Junmai.

sentences.zh: 十月，揆以行省兵三萬出潁、壽，史乂搭為驍騎將中軍副統，克安豐軍，戰霍丘、花靨，功居多。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Kui led thirty thousand provincial troops out from Ying and Shou; Shiguda served as Deputy Commander-in-chief of the center army among the fierce cavalry generals, took Anfeng Army, and fought at Huoqiu and Huayan — his merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, Kui led thirty thousand provincial troops out from Ying and Shou. Shiguda served as deputy commander-in-chief of the center among the fierce cavalry generals, took Anfeng Army, and fought at Huoqiu and Huayan — his merit was greatest.

sentences.zh: 十二月，從攻和州，中流矢卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, while following the attack on Hezhou, he was struck by a flying arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, while following the attack on Hezhou, he was struck by a flying arrow and died.

sentences.zh: 史乂搭形不過中人，而拳勇善鬥，所用槍長二丈，軍中號為「長槍副統」。

translations.literal: Shiguda's stature was no more than middling, yet he was bold in fist-fighting and skilled in combat; the spear he used was two zhang long, and in the army he was called "Deputy Commander Long Spear."
translations.idiomatic: Shiguda was of no more than middling stature, yet he was bold in hand-to-hand fighting and skilled in combat. The spear he used was two zhang long, and in the army he was called "Deputy Commander Long Spear."

sentences.zh: 又工用手箭，箭長不盈握，每用百數，散置鎧中，遇敵抽箭，以鞭揮之，或以指鉗取飛擲，數矢齊發，無不中，敵以為神。

translations.literal: He was also skilled with hand-arrows; the arrows were less than a handspan long. He used them by the hundreds, scattering them in his armor; when he met the enemy he would draw an arrow, lash it with his whip, or pinch it with his fingers and hurl it — several arrows flying together, none missing. The enemy considered it divine.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled with hand-arrows no longer than a handspan. He carried them by the hundreds, scattered in his armor; when he met the enemy he would draw an arrow, lash it with his whip, or pinch it with his fingers and hurl it — several arrows flying together, none missing. The enemy thought it divine.

sentences.zh: 其箭皆以智創，雖子弟亦不能傳其法。

translations.literal: His arrows were all devised by his own ingenuity; even his sons and younger brothers could not transmit his method.
translations.idiomatic: His arrows were all devised by his own ingenuity; even his sons and younger brothers could not learn his method.

sentences.zh: 在北部守厭山營，敵尤畏之，不敢近。

translations.literal: When he guarded Yanshan Camp in the north, the enemy feared him especially and did not dare approach.
translations.idiomatic: When he guarded Yanshan Camp in the north, the enemy feared him especially and did not dare approach.

sentences.zh: 及死，將士皆惋惜之。

translations.literal: When he died, officers and soldiers all lamented him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, officers and soldiers all lamented his loss.

sentences.zh: 世宗謂宰臣曰：「宗浩有才幹，可及者無幾。」

translations.literal: Shizong said to the chief ministers: "Zong Hao has talent and ability; few can match him."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong said to the chief ministers: "Zong Hao has talent and ability; few can match him."

sentences.zh: 二十三年，征為大理卿，逾年授山東路統軍使，兼知益都府事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was summoned as Grand Judge of the Court of Judicial Review; after a year he was appointed Commander of the Shandong Route Army and concurrently Administrator of Yidu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was summoned as Grand Judge of the Court of Judicial Review. After a year he was appointed Commander of the Shandong Route Army and concurrently Administrator of Yidu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，世宗諭之曰：「卿年尚少，以卿近屬，有治跡，故以此授卿，宜體朕意。」

translations.literal: On taking leave at audience, Shizong instructed him, saying: "You are still young; because you are a close kinsman and have a record of governance, I therefore appoint you to this — you should embody my intent."
translations.idiomatic: On taking leave at audience, Shizong told him: "You are still young. Because you are a close kinsman with a record of governance, I appoint you to this post — you should embody my intent."

sentences.zh: 因賜金帶遣之。

translations.literal: He then granted a gold belt and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted him a gold belt and sent him off.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，為賜宋主趙甗生日使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he served as envoy to convey birthday congratulations to the Song ruler Zhao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he served as envoy to convey birthday congratulations to the Song ruler Zhao Yan.

sentences.zh: 還，授刑部尚書，俄拜參知政事。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Minister of Punishments; soon afterward he was appointed Associate Administrator of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Minister of Punishments, and soon afterward Associate Administrator of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，出為北京留守，三轉同判大睦親府事。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong took the throne, he went out as Defender of the Northern Capital and was transferred three times to Associate Director of the Office of Imperial Clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong acceded, he went out as Defender of the Northern Capital and was transferred three times to Associate Director of the Office of Imperial Clansmen.

sentences.zh: 北方有警，命宗浩佩金虎符駐泰州便宜從事。

translations.literal: When there was alarm in the north, Zong Hao was ordered to wear the gold tiger tally and station at Taizhou with discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: When there was alarm in the north, Zong Hao was ordered to wear the gold tiger tally and station at Taizhou with discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 朝廷發上京等路軍萬人以戍。

translations.literal: The court dispatched ten thousand troops from the Shangjing Route and other circuits to garrison the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched ten thousand troops from the Shangjing Route and other circuits to garrison the frontier.

sentences.zh: 宗浩以糧儲未備，且度敵未敢動，遂分其軍就食隆、肇間。

translations.literal: Zong Hao, because grain stores were not yet prepared and he judged that the enemy would not dare move, then divided the army to forage between Long and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Because grain stores were not yet prepared and he judged the enemy would not dare move, Zong Hao divided the army to forage between Long and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 是冬，果無警。

translations.literal: That winter, indeed there was no alarm.
translations.idiomatic: That winter there was indeed no alarm.

sentences.zh: 北部廣吉剌者尤桀驁，屢脅諸部入塞。

translations.literal: The Guangjila of the northern frontier were especially fierce and unruly, repeatedly coercing various tribes to enter the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangjila of the northern frontier were especially fierce and unruly, repeatedly coercing various tribes to raid across the border.

sentences.zh: 宗浩請乘其春暮馬弱擊之。

translations.literal: Zong Hao requested to strike them when their horses were weak in late spring.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Hao requested to strike them when their horses were weak in late spring.

sentences.zh: 時阻珝亦叛，內族襄行省事於北京，詔議其事。

translations.literal: At that time Zuxu had also rebelled; the inner-clan Xiang held provincial authority at the Northern Capital, and an edict was issued to deliberate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zuxu had also rebelled. Inner-clan Xiang held provincial authority at the Northern Capital, and an edict was issued to deliberate the matter.

sentences.zh: 襄以謂若攻破廣吉剌，則阻珝無東顧憂，不若留之，以牽其勢。

translations.literal: Xiang held that if Guangjila were broken, Zuxu would have no worry of looking east, and it would be better to leave them to tie down his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang argued that if Guangjila were destroyed, Zuxu would have no need to watch his eastern flank, and it would be better to leave Guangjila in place to tie down his strength.

sentences.zh: 宗浩奏：「國家以堂堂之勢，不能掃滅小部，顧欲藉彼為捍乎？

translations.literal: Zong Hao memorialized: "Our state, with its imposing power, cannot sweep away a small tribe — and yet wishes to rely on them as a shield?
translations.idiomatic: Zong Hao memorialized: "Our state, with all its imposing power, cannot sweep away a small tribe — and yet wishes to rely on them as a shield?

sentences.zh: 臣請先破廣吉剌，然後提兵北滅阻珝。」

translations.literal: Your subject requests first to break Guangjila, then to lead troops north and destroy Zuxu."
translations.idiomatic: I request first to break Guangjila, then to lead troops north and destroy Zuxu."

sentences.zh: 章再上，從之。

translations.literal: After he memorialized again, the court assented.
translations.idiomatic: After he memorialized again, the court assented.

sentences.zh: 詔諭宗浩曰：「將征北部，固卿之誠，更宜加意，毋致後悔。」

translations.literal: An edict instructed Zong Hao, saying: "In campaigning against the northern frontier, your loyalty is firm — you should be all the more careful and not bring later regret."
translations.idiomatic: An edict instructed Zong Hao: "In campaigning against the northern frontier, your loyalty is firm — be all the more careful and leave no cause for later regret."

sentences.zh: 宗浩覘知合底忻與婆速火等相結，廣吉剌之勢必分，彼既畏我見討，而複掣肘仇敵，則理必求降，可呼致也。

translations.literal: Zong Hao observed and knew that Hedi Xin had joined with Pasuo Huo and others; Guangjila's strength would necessarily be divided. They would both fear our punitive expedition and be checked by hostile tribes — then by reason they would necessarily seek to surrender, and could be summoned in.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Hao observed that Hedi Xin had joined with Pasuo Huo and others, so Guangjila's strength would necessarily be divided. They would both fear our punitive expedition and be checked by hostile tribes — then by reason they would necessarily seek to surrender, and could be summoned in.

sentences.zh: 因遣主簿撒領軍二百為先鋒，戒之曰：「若廣吉剌降，可就征其兵以圖合底忻，仍偵餘部所在，速使來報，大軍當進，與汝擊破之必矣。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Chief Clerk Sa to lead two hundred troops as vanguard, admonishing him, saying: "If Guangjila surrenders, you may then levy their troops to strike at Hedi Xin. Still reconnoiter where the remaining tribes are located and swiftly send word back. The main army will advance — together with you we will certainly smash them."
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Chief Clerk Sa ahead with two hundred troops as vanguard, instructing him: "If Guangjila submits, levy their forces at once and move against Hedi Xin. Keep scouting the whereabouts of the other tribes and report back quickly. The main army will advance — with your help we are sure to break them."

sentences.zh: 合底忻者，與山只昆皆北方別部，恃強中立，無所羈屬，往來阻珝、廣吉剌間，連歲擾邊，皆二部為之也。

translations.literal: Hedi Xin and Shan Zhikun were both separate tribes of the northern frontier. Relying on their strength, they stood neutral and submitted to no one. Moving back and forth between Zuxu and Guangjila, for years they had harassed the borders — both tribes were responsible for this.
translations.idiomatic: Hedi Xin and Shan Zhikun were independent northern tribes that relied on their strength to stay neutral, bound to no overlord. Roaming between Zuxu and Guangjila, they had raided the frontier year after year — the two of them were behind it all.

sentences.zh: 撒入敵境，廣吉剌果降，遂征其兵萬四千騎，馳報以待。

translations.literal: Sa entered enemy territory; Guangjila did indeed surrender. He then levied fourteen thousand of their horsemen and sent a swift report to await the main force.
translations.idiomatic: Sa crossed into enemy country; Guangjila surrendered as expected. He mustered fourteen thousand of their horsemen and sent a fast courier to await the main army.

sentences.zh: 宗浩北進，命人齎三十日糧，報撒會于移米河共擊敵，而所遣人誤入婆速火部，由是東軍失期。

translations.literal: Zong Hao advanced north, ordering men to carry thirty days' rations and notify Sa to rendezvous at the Yimi River for a joint strike against the enemy. But the messenger sent went astray into Pasuo Huo territory; consequently the eastern army missed its rendezvous.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Hao marched north, sending men with thirty days' rations to tell Sa to meet at the Yimi River for a combined attack. The courier went astray into Pasuo Huo territory instead, and the eastern force missed its rendezvous.

sentences.zh: 宗浩前軍至忒里葛山，遇山只昆所統石魯、渾灘兩部，擊走之，斬首千二百級，俘生口車畜甚眾。

translations.literal: Zong Hao's van reached Telige Mountain and encountered the Shilu and Hundan tribes under Shan Zhikun's command. He routed them, beheading twelve hundred and capturing many people, carts, and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Hao's vanguard reached Telige Mountain and met the Shilu and Hundan tribes under Shan Zhikun. He drove them off, taking twelve hundred heads and large numbers of captives, carts, and livestock.

sentences.zh: 進至呼歇水，敵勢大蹙，於是合底忻部長白古帶、山只昆部長胡必剌及婆速火所遣和火者皆乞降。

translations.literal: Advancing to the Huxie River, the enemy's position was greatly pressed. Thereupon Hedi Xin's chieftain Baigudai, Shan Zhikun's chieftain Hubila, and the Hehuo envoy sent by Pasuo Huo all begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on to the Huxie River, he cornered the enemy. Hedi Xin's chieftain Baigudai, Shan Zhikun's chieftain Hubila, and the Hehuo envoy sent by Pasuo Huo all pleaded to surrender.

sentences.zh: 宗浩承詔，諭而釋之。

translations.literal: Acting on imperial decree, Zong Hao instructed them and released them.
translations.idiomatic: Following the imperial order, Zong Hao admonished them and set them free.

sentences.zh: 胡必剌因言，所部迪列土近在移米河不肯偕降，乞討之。

translations.literal: Hubila then said that his subordinate Dielie Tu was close by the Yimi River and refused to surrender together with them, and requested permission to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Hubila then reported that his subordinate Dielie Tu, camped near the Yimi River, would not submit with the rest, and asked leave to attack him.

sentences.zh: 乃移軍趨移米，與迪列土遇，擊之，斬首三百級，赴水死者十四五，獲牛羊萬二千，車帳稱是。

translations.literal: He then shifted the army toward Yimi, met Dielie Tu, and attacked. Three hundred heads were taken; four or five out of ten who fled into the water drowned. Cattle and sheep numbering twelve thousand were seized, with carts and tents in like abundance.
translations.idiomatic: He moved the army toward Yimi, met Dielie Tu, and struck. Three hundred heads were taken; four or five in ten of those who fled into the river drowned. They seized twelve thousand cattle and sheep, with carts and tents in proportion.

sentences.zh: 合底忻等恐大軍至，西渡移米，棄輜重遁去。

translations.literal: Fearing the arrival of the main army, Hedi Xin and the others crossed the Yimi to the west, abandoning their baggage and fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: Hedi Xin and the others, fearing the main force, crossed the Yimi to the west, abandoning their baggage train and fleeing.

sentences.zh: 撒與廣吉剌部長忒里虎追躡及之，於窊里不水縱擊大破之。

translations.literal: Sa and Guangjila's chieftain Telihu pursued and caught up with them, and at the Wali Bu River launched an attack that broke them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Sa and Guangjila's chieftain Telihu pursued, caught them at the Wali Bu River, and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 婆速火九部斬首、溺水死者四千五百餘人，獲駝馬牛羊不可勝計。

translations.literal: Among the nine Pasuo Huo tribes, those beheaded and drowned totaled more than forty-five hundred. Camels, horses, cattle, and sheep captured were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Among the nine Pasuo Huo tribes, more than forty-five hundred were killed or drowned. Camels, horses, cattle, and sheep taken were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 軍還，婆速火乞內屬，並請置吏。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Pasuo Huo petitioned to be incorporated within the empire and requested that officials be installed.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return, Pasuo Huo asked to come under imperial jurisdiction and requested the appointment of officials.

sentences.zh: 上優詔褒諭，遷光祿大夫，以所獲馬六千置牧以處之。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a gracious edict of praise and commendation, promoted him to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and established pastures with six thousand horses from the spoils to settle them there.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a gracious edict of commendation, promoted Zong Hao to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and set aside pastures with six thousand captured horses to settle the tribe.

sentences.zh: 明年，宴賜東北部，尋拜樞密使，封榮國公。

translations.literal: The next year he was feasted and rewarded in the northeastern frontier. Soon after he was appointed Military Affairs Commissioner and enfeoffed as Duke of Glory State.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was feasted and rewarded on the northeastern frontier. Soon after he was made Military Affairs Commissioner and enfeoffed Duke of Glory State.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷置東北路招討司泰州，去境三百里，每敵入，比出兵追襲，敵已遁去。

translations.literal: Initially the court had placed the Northeast Route Pacification Commission at Taizhou, three hundred li from the border. Whenever enemies entered, by the time troops sallied in pursuit, the enemy had already fled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had placed the Northeast Route Pacification Commission at Taizhou, three hundred li from the border. Whenever raiders came in, troops set out in pursuit only after the enemy had already gone.

sentences.zh: 至是，宗浩奏徙之金山，以據要害，設副招討二員，分置左右，由是敵不敢犯。

translations.literal: At this time Zong Hao memorialized to move it to Jinshan to hold the strategic points, with two deputy pacification commissioners appointed and posted on the left and right. From this the enemy did not dare violate the border.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Hao now memorialized to move the commission to Jinshan to hold the key passes, with two deputy pacification commissioners posted on the left and right. After that the enemy no longer dared raid.

sentences.zh: 會中都、山東、河北屯駐軍人地土不贍，官田多為民所冒占，命宗浩行省事，詣諸道括籍，凡得地三十余萬頃。

translations.literal: As garrison soldiers in the Central Capital, Shandong, and Hebei had insufficient land allotments and much official land had been encroached upon by commoners, Zong Hao was ordered as provisional provincial commissioner to go to the various circuits and register land — more than three hundred thousand qing in all were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Because garrison troops in the Central Capital, Shandong, and Hebei lacked adequate land and much official farmland had been seized by commoners, Zong Hao was sent as provisional provincial commissioner to register holdings in every circuit. More than three hundred thousand qing were recovered.

sentences.zh: 還，坐以倡女自隨，為憲司所糾，出知真定府事。

translations.literal: On his return he was impeached by the censorate for keeping singing girls with him on tour and was demoted to prefect of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the censorate impeached him for traveling with singing girls; he was demoted to prefect of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 徙西京留守，複為樞密使，進拜尚書右丞相，超授崇進。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Western Capital commandant, again made Military Affairs Commissioner, promoted to Right Chief Councilor of the Secretariat, and granted the extraordinary rank of Chongjin.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to commandant of the Western Capital, again made Military Affairs Commissioner, promoted to Right Chief Councilor, and granted the extraordinary rank of Chongjin.

sentences.zh: 時懲北邊不寧，議築壕壘以備守戍，廷臣多異同。

translations.literal: At the time, chastened by unrest on the northern frontier, there was discussion of building moats and ramparts for frontier defense; court ministers held widely differing views.
translations.idiomatic: Troubled by northern frontier unrest, the court debated building moats and ramparts for defense; ministers sharply disagreed.

sentences.zh: 平章政事張萬公力言其不可，宗浩獨謂便，乃命宗浩行省事，以督其役。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Zhang Wannong strongly argued against it, but Zong Hao alone held it expedient. Zong Hao was then ordered as provisional provincial commissioner to oversee the work.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Zhang Wannong argued forcefully against it, but Zong Hao alone favored the plan. Zong Hao was then sent as provisional provincial commissioner to supervise the project.

sentences.zh: 功畢，上賜詔褒賚甚厚。

translations.literal: When the work was complete, the emperor bestowed an edict with rich praise and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, the emperor issued an edict with lavish praise and rewards.

sentences.zh: 撒里部長陀括里入塞，宗浩以兵追躡，與僕散揆軍合擊之，殺獲甚眾，敵遁去。

translations.literal: The Sar chieftain Tuotuoli entered the passes. Zong Hao pursued with troops and joined Pusan Kui's army in a combined attack, killing and capturing in great numbers as the enemy fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sar chieftain Tuotuoli raided across the border. Zong Hao pursued and joined Pusan Kui's force in a combined strike, killing and capturing heavily before the enemy escaped.

sentences.zh: 詔征還，入見，優詔獎諭，躐遷儀同三司，賜玉束帶一、金器百兩、重幣二十端，進拜左丞相。

translations.literal: He was recalled by edict, received in audience, and honored with a gracious edict of commendation. He was promoted in one step to Honorary Director of the Three Highest Offices, given one jade waist-strap set, a hundred taels of gold vessels, twenty bolts of heavy silks, and advanced to Left Chief Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled by edict, he was received in audience and honored with a gracious commendation. He was promoted in one step to Honorary Director of the Three Highest Offices, given a jade waist-strap set, a hundred taels of gold vessels, twenty bolts of heavy silks, and advanced to Left Chief Councilor.

sentences.zh: 宋人畔盟，王師南伐，會平章政事揆病，乃命宗浩兼都元帥往督進討。

translations.literal: When the Song broke the treaty and the imperial army marched south, Grand Councilor Kui fell ill. Zong Hao was then ordered to serve additionally as Grand Marshal and go supervise the advance and punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song broke the treaty and the imperial army marched south, Grand Councilor Kui fell ill. Zong Hao was ordered to serve additionally as Grand Marshal and supervise the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 宗浩馳至汴，大張兵勢，親赴襄陽巡師而還。

translations.literal: Zong Hao galloped to Bian, greatly displayed military might, personally went to Xiangyang to inspect the troops, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Hao raced to Bian, put on a great show of force, personally inspected the troops at Xiangyang, and returned.

sentences.zh: 宋人大懼，乃命知樞密院事張岩以書乞和。

translations.literal: The Song were greatly terrified and ordered Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zhang Yan to write begging for peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Song were terrified and had Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zhang Yan write to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 宗浩以辭旨未順卻之，仍諭以稱臣、割地、縛送元謀奸臣等事。

translations.literal: Zong Hao rejected the letter because its wording was not deferential, and still instructed them regarding submission as a subject state, cession of territory, and binding and sending the chief culprits among the traitors.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Hao rejected the letter for its insufficient deference and reiterated his demands: submission, cession of territory, and the binding and delivery of the chief traitors.

sentences.zh: 岩複遣方信孺齎其主趙擴誓稿來，且言擴併發三使，將賀天壽節及通謝，仍報其祖母謝氏殂，致書于都元帥宗浩曰：

translations.literal: Zhang Yan again sent Fang Xinru bearing his lord Zhao Kuo's draft oath of allegiance. He also said Zhao Kuo would dispatch three envoys together to congratulate the Heavenly Longevity Festival and convey thanks, and reported the death of his grandmother, Lady Xie — writing to Grand Marshal Zong Hao as follows:
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan sent Fang Xinru again with his sovereign Zhao Kuo's draft oath. He also said Zhao Kuo would dispatch three envoys together to congratulate the Heavenly Longevity Festival and offer thanks, and reported the death of his grandmother Lady Xie — addressing Grand Marshal Zong Hao as follows:

sentences.zh: 方信孺還，遠貽報翰及所承鈞旨，仰見以生靈休息為重，曲示包容矜軫之意。

translations.literal: Fang Xinru has returned, bearing from afar your written reply and the instructions you conveyed. I look up and see that you place rest for the people above all else, graciously showing a spirit of forbearance and compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xinru has returned with your distant reply and the instructions you conveyed. I see that you put the people's rest above all else, graciously showing forbearance and compassion.

sentences.zh: 聞命踴躍，私竊自喜，即具奏聞，備述大金皇帝天覆地載之仁，與都元帥海涵春育之德。

translations.literal: Upon receiving your command I leapt for joy and privately rejoiced. I immediately memorialized in full, describing the Grand Jin emperor's mercy that covers heaven and bears up the earth, and the Grand Marshal's virtue vast as the sea, nurturing as spring.
translations.idiomatic: On receiving your word I rejoiced openly and in private. I memorialized at once, describing the Grand Jin emperor's mercy that covers heaven and upholds earth, and the Grand Marshal's virtue as vast as the sea and nurturing as spring.

sentences.zh: 旋奉上旨，亟遣信使通謝宸庭，仍先令信孺再詣行省，以請定議。

translations.literal: I then received my sovereign's order to send trusted envoys at once to thank the imperial court, and first to send Fang Xinru again to the field headquarters to request a final settlement.
translations.idiomatic: I then received my sovereign's order to send trusted envoys at once to thank the imperial court, and to send Fang Xinru again to the field headquarters first to seek a final settlement.

sentences.zh: 區區之愚，實恃高明，必蒙洞照，重布本末，幸垂聽焉。

translations.literal: This small-minded one's humble thoughts rely entirely on your enlightened understanding, which I trust will see all clearly. I set forth the whole story once more and beg you to lend your ear.
translations.idiomatic: In my small way I rely on your enlightened judgment, which I trust will see everything clearly. I set out the whole account once more and beg you to hear me.

sentences.zh: 兵端之開，雖本朝失於輕信，然痛罪奸臣之蔽欺，亦不為不早。

translations.literal: Though the opening of hostilities stemmed from our court's failure of credulous trust, our painful punishment of the traitorous ministers who deceived and concealed was not untimely.
translations.idiomatic: Though war began because our court trusted too easily, we did not delay in punishing the traitorous ministers who deceived us.

sentences.zh: 自去歲五月，編竄鄧友龍，六月又誅蘇師旦等。

translations.literal: From last year, in the fifth month Deng Youlong was banished to a remote post; in the sixth month Su Shidan and others were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Last year, in the fifth month Deng Youlong was banished; in the sixth month Su Shidan and others were executed.

sentences.zh: 是時大國尚未嘗一出兵也，本朝即捐已得之泗州，諸軍屯於境外者盡令徹戍而南，悔艾之誠，於茲可見。

translations.literal: At that time your great state had not yet moved a single soldier. Our court immediately surrendered Sizhou, which it had already taken; all armies encamped beyond the border were fully withdrawn south. The sincerity of our remorse is visible in this.
translations.idiomatic: At that time your great state had not yet marched a single soldier. Our court gave up Sizhou, which we had already taken, and ordered every army camped beyond the border to withdraw south. Our remorse should be plain from this.

sentences.zh: 惟是名分之諭，今昔事殊，本朝皇帝本無佳兵之意，況關係至重，又豈臣子之所敢言？

translations.literal: As for your instruction on ceremonial status — past and present circumstances differ. Our emperor has never been one to delight in war. Moreover the matter touches the utmost gravity — how could any subject dare speak of it?
translations.idiomatic: As for your instruction on ceremonial status, past and present are not the same. Our emperor has never delighted in war. The matter is too grave — how could any subject dare speak of it?

sentences.zh: 江外之地，恃為遮罩，儻如來諭，何以為國？

translations.literal: The lands south of the river we rely on as a protective screen. If we did as you instruct, how could we maintain our state?
translations.idiomatic: We rely on the lands south of the river as our shield. If we did as you ask, how could we remain a state?

sentences.zh: 大朝所當念察。

translations.literal: Your great dynasty should take this into consideration.
translations.idiomatic: Your great dynasty should weigh this carefully.

sentences.zh: 至於首事人鄧友龍等誤國之罪，固無所逃，若使執縛以送，是本朝不得自致其罰於臣下。

translations.literal: As for the guilt of the chief instigators such as Deng Youlong for misleading the state — that cannot be evaded. Yet if we were made to bind and send them, our court would be unable to impose its own punishments upon its subjects.
translations.idiomatic: The guilt of the chief instigators such as Deng Youlong for misleading the state cannot be denied. Yet if we were forced to bind and deliver them, our court would be unable to punish its own subjects itself.

sentences.zh: 所有歲幣，前書已增大定所減之數，此在上國，初何足以為重輕，特欲藉手以見謝過之實。

translations.literal: Regarding the annual tribute, our earlier letter already added back what had been reduced in the Dading agreement. To your great state this was never a matter of weight or lightness — we only wished to use it as a means to show the sincerity of our apology.
translations.idiomatic: On annual tribute, our earlier letter already restored what had been cut in the Dading agreement. To your great state this was never a question of more or less — we only meant to show the sincerity of our apology.

sentences.zh: 儻上國諒此至情，物之多寡，必不深計。

translations.literal: If your great state understands this genuine feeling, you will surely not reckon deeply whether the goods are many or few.
translations.idiomatic: If your great state understands our true feeling, you will surely not quibble over the amount.

sentences.zh: 矧惟兵興以來，連歲創殘，賦入屢蠲，若又重取於民，豈基元元無窮之困，竊計大朝亦必有所不忍也。

translations.literal: Moreover, since the outbreak of war, year after year the people have been ravaged and tax levies repeatedly remitted. If tribute were again heavily extracted from the people, how could the common folk not be boundlessly impoverished? I venture to think your great dynasty would also be unable to bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since war began the people have been ravaged year after year and taxes repeatedly remitted. To levy heavily again would only bind the common folk in endless hardship — I trust your great dynasty would also find that unbearable.

sentences.zh: 于通謝禮幣之外，別致微誠，庶幾以此易彼。

translations.literal: Beyond the gifts for thanks and greeting, we offer this small sincerity — hoping thereby to exchange one thing for another.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the gifts of thanks and greeting, we offer this small token of sincerity, hoping to exchange one concession for another.

sentences.zh: 其歸投之人，皆雀鼠偷生，一時竄匿，往往不知存亡，本朝既無所用，豈以去來為意。

translations.literal: Those who fled to your side were all like sparrows and rats clinging to life, hiding for a time — often with no knowledge whether they still live or die. Our court has no use for them; why should we care whether they come or go?
translations.idiomatic: Those who fled to your side were sparrows and rats clinging to life, hiding for a time — often with no knowledge of whether they still live. Our court has no use for them; why should we care whether they come or go?

sentences.zh: 當隆興時，固有大朝名族貴將南來者，洎和議之定，亦嘗約各不取索，況茲瑣瑣，誠何足雲。

translations.literal: At the time of the Longxing peace, eminent families and honored generals of your great dynasty did come south. When the treaty was settled, it was also agreed that neither side would demand their return — much less such trivial persons as these. Truly they are not worth mentioning.
translations.idiomatic: At the Longxing peace, eminent families and honored generals of your dynasty did come south. When the treaty was settled, both sides agreed not to demand their return — much less such petty persons. They are hardly worth mentioning.

sentences.zh: 儻大朝必欲追求，尚容拘刷。

translations.literal: If your great dynasty must pursue them, we can still make arrests and turn them over.
translations.idiomatic: If your great dynasty insists on pursuing them, we can still hunt them down and hand them over.

sentences.zh: 至如泗州等處驅掠人，悉當護送歸業。

translations.literal: As for people driven off and plundered from places such as Sizhou — all shall be escorted home to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: As for people driven off and plundered from places such as Sizhou, all shall be escorted home to resume their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 夫締新好者不念舊惡，成大功者不較小利。

translations.literal: In forging a new friendship one does not dwell on old wrongs; in accomplishing great deeds one does not haggle over small gains.
translations.idiomatic: Those who forge new friendship do not dwell on old wrongs; those who accomplish great deeds do not haggle over small gains.

sentences.zh: 欲望力賜開陳，捐棄前過，闊略他事，玉帛交馳，歡好如初，海內寧謐，長無軍兵之事。

translations.literal: We earnestly beg you to plead our cause with all your strength — to discard past faults, set aside other matters, and let silks and gifts pass back and forth so that friendship is as before, the realm tranquil within the four seas, and armed conflict forever absent.
translations.idiomatic: We earnestly beg you to plead our cause — to set aside past faults and other disputes, let silks and gifts pass freely, restore friendship as before, bring peace to the realm, and keep armies forever sheathed.

sentences.zh: 功烈昭宣，德澤洋溢，鼎彝所紀，方冊所載，垂之萬世，豈有既乎！

translations.literal: Your achievements proclaimed abroad, your beneficence overflowing — what bronze vessels record and what official histories inscribe will endure for ten thousand generations without end!
translations.idiomatic: Your achievements proclaimed abroad, your grace overflowing — what bronze inscriptions record and official histories preserve will endure for ten thousand generations without end!

sentences.zh: 重惟大金皇帝誕節將臨，禮當修賀，兼之本國多故，又言合遣人使，接續津發，已具公移，企望取接。

translations.literal: We again reflect that the Grand Jin emperor's birthday draws near and courtesy requires us to offer congratulations. Our state has also had many troubles, and word has come that envoys should be dispatched. They have been sent in succession and official notices have been prepared — we look forward to your receiving them.
translations.idiomatic: We note again that the Grand Jin emperor's birthday draws near and courtesy requires our congratulations. Our state has also had many troubles, and we understand envoys should be sent in succession. Official notices have been prepared — we look forward to your receiving them.

sentences.zh: 伏冀鑒其至再至三有加無已之誠，亟踐請盟之諾，即底于成，感戴恩德永永無極。

translations.literal: We humbly hope you will discern our sincerity, repeated again and again without limit, and swiftly fulfill your promise to conclude a treaty — bringing matters to success. Our gratitude for your grace shall be boundless forever.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly hope you will see our sincerity, offered again and again without limit, and swiftly honor your promise to conclude peace. Our gratitude for your grace shall know no end.

sentences.zh: 誓書副本慮往復遷延，就以錄呈。

translations.literal: Lest the copy of the oath text be delayed in shuttle back and forth, we submit the transcript herewith.
translations.idiomatic: Lest the oath text be delayed in back-and-forth exchange, we submit a copy herewith.

sentences.zh: 初，信孺之來，自以和議遂成，輒自稱通謝使所參議官。

translations.literal: Initially, when Xinru came, he assumed the peace talks were settled and styled himself deliberation officer of the gratitude mission.
translations.idiomatic: When Xinru first arrived, he assumed peace was already settled and styled himself deliberation officer of the gratitude mission.

sentences.zh: 大定中，宋人乞和，以王抃為通問使所參議官，信孺援以為例。

translations.literal: In the Dading era, when the Song sought peace, Wang Pan had served as deliberation officer of the inquiry mission; Xinru cited this as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dading era, when the Song sought peace, Wang Pan had served as deliberation officer of the inquiry mission — Xinru cited this as precedent.

sentences.zh: 宗浩怒其輕妄，囚之以聞。

translations.literal: Zong Hao, angered by his presumption, imprisoned him and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Hao, angered by his presumption, imprisoned him and reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 朝廷亦以其為行人而不能孚兩國之情，將留之，遣使問宗浩。

translations.literal: The court also considered that as an envoy he failed to inspire mutual trust between the two states and planned to detain him. They sent a messenger to ask Zong Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The court also judged that as an envoy he had failed to inspire trust between the two states and planned to detain him. They sent a messenger to consult Zong Hao.

sentences.zh: 宗浩曰：「今信孺事既未集，自知還必得罪，拘之適使他日有以藉口。

translations.literal: Zong Hao said: "Now Xinru's mission has not succeeded. He knows that on returning he will certainly be punished. Detaining him would only give him an excuse on some future day.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Hao said: "Xinru's mission has not succeeded. He knows he will be punished on his return. Detaining him would only give him an excuse later.

sentences.zh: 不若數其恌易，而釋遣之使歸，自窮無辭以白其國人，則擴、侂胄必擇謹厚者來矣。」

translations.literal: Better to enumerate his frivolous improprieties and release him to return home. Having no words with which to justify himself to his countrymen, Kuo and Tuozhou will surely choose someone sober and reliable next time."
translations.idiomatic: Better to list his frivolous offenses and send him home. With no way to justify himself to his countrymen, Kuo and Tuozhou will surely choose someone sober and reliable next time."

sentences.zh: 於是遣之，而複張岩書曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent him off, and again wrote to Zhang Yan:
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he released him, and wrote again to Zhang Yan:

sentences.zh: 方信孺重以書來，詳味其辭，於請和之意雖若婉遜，而所畫之事猶未悉從，惟言當還泗州等驅掠而已。

translations.literal: Fang Xinru has again sent a letter. Pondering his words carefully: though his tone in seeking peace seems mild and deferential, on the matters laid out he has not fully complied — he speaks only of returning those driven off and plundered from Sizhou and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xinru has written again. Reading his words closely: though his tone in seeking peace seems mild and deferential, he has not fully complied on the matters at issue — he speaks only of returning those driven off and plundered from Sizhou and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 至於責貢幣，則欲以舊數為增，追叛亡，則欲以橫恩為例，而稱臣、割地、縛送奸臣三事，則並飾虛說，弗肯如約。

translations.literal: On demanding tribute, he wishes to treat the old quota as an increase; on pursuing fugitive defectors, he wishes to cite the precedent of the Longxing agreement; and on the three matters of submission, cession of territory, and binding and sending the traitors — he dresses up empty words and refuses to comply as agreed.
translations.idiomatic: On tribute he treats the old quota as an increase; on fugitive defectors he cites the Longxing precedent; and on submission, cession of territory, and binding and sending the traitors — he offers empty words and refuses to comply.

sentences.zh: 豈以為朝廷過求有不可從，將度德量力，足以背城借一，與我軍角一日勝負者哉？

translations.literal: Does he imagine that the court's demands are excessive beyond what can be granted, and that measuring virtue and strength he could hold a city for a last stand and contest a single day's victory against our army?
translations.idiomatic: Does he think the court asks too much, and that measuring his strength he could hold a city for one last stand and fight our army for a single day's victory?

sentences.zh: 既不能強，又不能弱，不深思熟慮以計將來之利害，徒以不情之語形於尺牘而勤郵傳，何也？

translations.literal: Neither strong enough to resist nor weak enough to submit outright — without deep thought on future gain and loss, he merely puts unreasonable words on paper and keeps the couriers busy. What is the point?
translations.idiomatic: Neither strong enough to resist nor weak enough to submit — without weighing future gain and loss, he merely puts unreasonable words on paper and keeps the couriers running. What is the point?

sentences.zh: 兵者兇器，佳之不祥，然聖人不得已而用之，故三皇、五帝所不能免。

translations.literal: Weapons are instruments of slaughter; to delight in them is ill-omened. Yet sages employ them only when they must — therefore even the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors could not avoid war.
translations.idiomatic: Weapons are instruments of slaughter; to delight in them is ill-omened. Yet sages use them only when they must — even the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors could not avoid war.

sentences.zh: 夫豈不以生靈為念，蓋犯順負義有不可恕者。

translations.literal: This is surely not because they cared nothing for the people; there are crimes of rebellion against righteousness that cannot be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: That is not because they cared nothing for the people; some crimes of rebellion and faithlessness cannot be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 乃者彼國犯盟，侵我疆埸，帥府奉命征討，雖未及出師，姑以逐處戍兵，隨宜捍禦，所向摧破，莫之敢當，執俘折馘，不可勝計，餘眾震懾靡然奔潰。

translations.literal: Recently their state broke the treaty and violated our borders. The marshal's headquarters, receiving orders to campaign, though the main army had not yet marched out, relied on garrison troops at each post to defend as circumstances allowed — smashing whatever they met, none daring to resist. Prisoners taken and heads severed were beyond counting; the rest were struck with terror and fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Recently their state broke the treaty and violated our borders. The marshal's headquarters, ordered to campaign, had not yet marched the main army out, but garrison troops at each post defended as they could — crushing every foe, none daring to stand. Captives and severed heads were beyond counting; the rest fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 是以所侵疆土，旋即底平，爰及泗州，亦不勞而複。

translations.literal: Thus the territory they had violated was quickly pacified; even Sizhou was recovered without effort.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the territory they had violated was quickly pacified; even Sizhou was retaken without effort.

sentences.zh: 今乃自謂捐其已得，斂軍徹戍，以為悔過之效，是豈誠實之言！

translations.literal: Now they claim to have relinquished what they had gained and withdrawn armies and garrisons as proof of repentance — how can this be honest speech!
translations.idiomatic: Now they claim to have given up what they had gained and withdrawn their armies and garrisons as proof of repentance — how can that be honest!

sentences.zh: 據陝西宣撫司申報，今夏宋人犯邊者十餘次，並為我軍擊退，梟斬捕獲，蓋以億計。

translations.literal: According to the Shaanxi Pacification Commission's report, this summer the Song violated the border more than ten times — all were beaten back by our troops; those beheaded, captured, or taken alive numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Shaanxi Pacification Commission, this summer the Song violated the border more than ten times — all were beaten back; those killed or captured numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 夫以悔艾罪咎，移書往來丐和之間，乃暗遣賊徒突我守圉，冀乘其不虞，以徼幸毫末，然則所為來請和者，理安在哉！

translations.literal: While professing remorse for their crimes and exchanging letters begging for peace, they secretly send raiders to break through our defenses, hoping to catch us unaware and snatch some petty gain — then what logic is there in their coming to sue for peace!
translations.idiomatic: While professing remorse and exchanging letters begging for peace, they secretly send raiders against our defenses, hoping to catch us off guard for some petty gain — then what sense is there in their coming to sue for peace!

sentences.zh: 其言名分之諭，今昔事殊者，蓋與大定之事固殊矣。

translations.literal: As for their claim that the instruction on ceremonial status differs from past and present — it is indeed wholly different from the Dading affair.
translations.idiomatic: As for their claim that ceremonial status differs from past and present — that is indeed wholly unlike the Dading affair.

sentences.zh: 本朝之于宋國，恩深德厚，莫可殫述，皇統謝章，可概見也。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's grace and beneficence toward the Song state are deep beyond telling; the submission document of the Huangtong era gives a general picture.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's grace toward the Song is deep beyond telling; the submission document of the Huangtong era gives a general picture.

sentences.zh: 至於世宗皇帝俯就和好，三十年間恩澤之渥，夫豈可忘？

translations.literal: As for Emperor Shizong bending to conclude peace, the overflowing grace of those thirty years — how could it be forgotten?
translations.idiomatic: As for Emperor Shizong bending to conclude peace, the overflowing grace of those thirty years — how could that be forgotten?

sentences.zh: 江表舊臣於我，大定之初，以失在正隆，致南服不定，故特施大惠，易為侄國，以鎮撫之。

translations.literal: The old ministers south of the river toward us — at the beginning of Dading, because the fault lay in the Zhenglong era and the southern realm was unsettled, we specially granted a great concession, altering their status to nephew-state, to pacify and soothe them.
translations.idiomatic: Toward the old ministers south of the river, at the beginning of Dading — because the fault lay in the Zhenglong era and the south was unsettled — we specially granted a great concession, changing their status to nephew-state to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 今以小犯大，曲在於彼，既以絕大定之好，則復舊稱臣，於理為宜。

translations.literal: Now the lesser offends the greater; the wrong lies with them. Having broken the friendship of Dading, to restore the old form of submission is only right in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Now the lesser offends the greater; the fault is theirs. Having broken the Dading friendship, restoring the old form of submission is only right.

sentences.zh: 若為非臣子所敢言，在皇統時何故敢言而今獨不敢，是又誠然乎哉！

translations.literal: If they say it is not something subjects may speak of — why did they dare speak of it in Huangtong yet dare not now? Is that truly credible!
translations.idiomatic: If they say subjects may not speak of it — why did they dare speak of it in Huangtong yet dare not now? Is that credible!

sentences.zh: 又謂江外之地將為遮罩，割之則無以為國。

translations.literal: They also say the lands south of the river serve as a protective screen and that ceding them would leave no state to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: They also say the lands south of the river are their shield and that ceding them would leave no state to speak of.

sentences.zh: 夫籓籬之固，當守信義，如不務此，雖長江之險，亦不可恃，區區兩淮之地，何足遮罩而為國哉！

translations.literal: The strength of a frontier barrier lies in keeping faith and righteousness. Without attending to this, even the Yangzi's peril cannot be relied upon — how could the mere lands of the two Huai suffice as a screen to sustain a state!
translations.idiomatic: A frontier's strength lies in keeping faith and righteousness. Without that, even the Yangzi's barrier cannot be relied on — how could the two Huai alone sustain a state as a shield!

sentences.zh: 昔江左六朝之時，淮南屢嘗屬中國矣。

translations.literal: In the days of the Six Dynasties south of the river, Huainan repeatedly belonged to the central realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the days of the Six Dynasties south of the river, Huainan repeatedly belonged to the central realm.

sentences.zh: 至後周顯德間，南唐李景獻廬、舒、蘄、黃，畫江為界，是亦皆能為國。

translations.literal: Down to the Xiande era of Later Zhou, Li Jing of Southern Tang ceded Lu, Shu, Qi, and Huang and drew the Yangzi as boundary — yet each was still able to maintain a state.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the Xiande era of Later Zhou, Li Jing of Southern Tang ceded Lu, Shu, Qi, and Huang and took the Yangzi as boundary — yet each side still maintained a state.

sentences.zh: 既有如此故實，則割地之事，亦奚不可！

translations.literal: With such historical precedents, how could cession of territory be impermissible!
translations.idiomatic: With such precedents in history, how could cession of territory be impermissible!

sentences.zh: 自我師出疆，所下州軍縣鎮已為我有，未下者即當割而獻之。

translations.literal: Since our army crossed the border, prefectures, armies, districts, and towns already taken are ours. Those not yet taken must be ceded and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Since our army crossed the border, prefectures, districts, and towns already taken are ours. Those not yet taken must be ceded and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 今方信孺齎到誓書，乃雲疆界並依大國皇統、彼之隆興年已畫為定，若是則既不言割彼之地，又翻欲得我之已有者，豈理也哉！

translations.literal: Now the oath text Fang Xinru brings says borders should follow those fixed in our Huangtong era and their Longxing year — if so, they speak neither of ceding their lands nor instead seek to take what is already ours. Where is the reason in that!
translations.idiomatic: Now the oath Fang Xinru brings says borders should follow those fixed in our Huangtong era and their Longxing year — if so, they speak neither of ceding their lands nor instead seek to take what is already ours. Where is the reason in that!

sentences.zh: 又來書雲通謝禮幣之外，別備錢一百萬貫，折金銀各三萬兩，專以塞再增幣之責，又雲歲幣添五萬兩疋，其言無可准。

translations.literal: Their letter also says that beyond gifts of thanks they separately prepare a million strings of cash, equivalent to thirty thousand taels each of gold and silver, solely to meet the demand for increased tribute; it further says the annual tribute adds fifty thousand taels and bolts — such words cannot be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Their letter also says that beyond gifts of thanks they separately prepare a million strings of cash, equivalent to thirty thousand taels each of gold and silver, solely to meet the demand for increased tribute; it further says annual tribute adds fifty thousand taels and bolts — such terms cannot be accepted.

sentences.zh: 況和議未定，輒前具載約，擬為誓書，又直報通謝等三番人使，其自專如是，豈協禮體。

translations.literal: Moreover, while peace is not yet settled, they presumptuously lay out terms in advance as a draft oath and directly announce three rounds of gratitude envoys — such self-willed conduct does not accord with diplomatic propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, while peace is not yet settled, they presumptuously lay out terms in advance as a draft oath and announce three rounds of gratitude envoys — such self-willed conduct violates diplomatic propriety.

sentences.zh: 此方信孺以求成自任，臆度上國，謂如此徑往，則事必可集，輕瀆誑紿，理不可容。

translations.literal: This is Fang Xinru taking success upon himself, guessing at the great state's mind and assuming that if he proceeded thus directly the matter would surely succeed — trifling with, deceiving, and misleading. Such conduct cannot be tolerated.
translations.idiomatic: This is Fang Xinru taking success upon himself, guessing at the great state's mind and assuming that if he proceeded directly the matter would surely succeed — trifling with, deceiving, and misleading us. Such conduct cannot be tolerated.

sentences.zh: 尋具奏聞，欽奉聖訓：「昔宣、靖之際，棄信背盟，我師問罪，嘗割三鎮以乞和。

translations.literal: A memorial was soon submitted, and the sacred instruction was received: "In the time of Xuanhe and Jingkang they broke faith and the treaty; our army demanded accounting. They once ceded three prefectures to beg for peace.
translations.idiomatic: A memorial was soon submitted, and the sacred instruction was received: "In the time of Xuanhe and Jingkang they broke faith and the treaty; our army demanded accounting. They once ceded three prefectures to beg for peace.

sentences.zh: 今既無故興兵，蔑棄信誓，雖盡獻江、淮之地，猶不足以自贖。

translations.literal: Now they have raised arms without cause and despised sworn pledges — even were they to surrender all the lands of the Jianghuai, it would still not suffice to redeem themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Now they have raised arms without cause and despised sworn pledges — even were they to surrender all the Jianghuai, it would still not suffice to redeem themselves.

sentences.zh: 況彼國嘗自言，叔父侄子與君臣父子略不相遠，如能依應稱臣，即許以江、淮之間取中為界。

translations.literal: Moreover their state once said that uncle-nephew and subject-sovereign relations are not greatly different. If they comply and call themselves subjects, they may have the middle line between Jianghuai as border.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover their state once said that uncle-nephew and subject-sovereign relations are not greatly different. If they comply and call themselves subjects, they may take the middle line between Jianghuai as border.

sentences.zh: 如欲世為子國，即當盡割淮南，直以大江為界。

translations.literal: If they wish to be a vassal state in perpetuity, they must cede all of Huainan and take the Great River alone as boundary.
translations.idiomatic: If they wish to be a vassal state forever, they must cede all of Huainan and take the Great River alone as boundary.

sentences.zh: 陝西邊面並以大軍已占為定據。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi frontier shall likewise be fixed according to what the great army has already occupied.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi frontier shall likewise be fixed according to what the great army has already occupied.

sentences.zh: 元謀奸臣必使縛送，緣彼懇欲自致其罰，可令函首以獻。

translations.literal: The chief-culprit traitors must be bound and sent — since they earnestly wish to impose their own punishment, they may be required to present the heads in cases.
translations.idiomatic: The chief-culprit traitors must be bound and sent — since they earnestly wish to punish themselves, they may be required to present the heads in cases.

sentences.zh: 外歲幣雖添五萬兩疋，止是複皇統舊額而已，安得為增？

translations.literal: Beyond this, the annual tribute though adding fifty thousand taels and bolts only restores the old Huangtong quota — how can that count as an increase?
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this, the fifty thousand taels and bolts they add to annual tribute only restore the old Huangtong quota — how can that count as an increase?

sentences.zh: 可令更添五萬兩疋，以表悔謝之實。

translations.literal: They may be ordered to add another fifty thousand taels and bolts to demonstrate the sincerity of repentance.
translations.idiomatic: They may be ordered to add another fifty thousand taels and bolts to show the sincerity of their repentance.

sentences.zh: 向汴陽乞和時嘗進賞軍之物，金五百萬兩、銀五千萬、表段里絹各一百萬、牛馬騾各一萬、駝一千、書五監。

translations.literal: When they previously sued for peace at Bianyang they offered goods to reward the army: five million taels of gold, fifty million of silver, a million bolts each of patterned silks and raw silk, ten thousand each of cattle, horses, and mules, a thousand camels, and five stud offices.
translations.idiomatic: When they previously sued for peace at Bianyang they offered goods to reward the army: five million taels of gold, fifty million of silver, a million bolts each of patterned silks and raw silk, ten thousand each of cattle, horses, and mules, a thousand camels, and five stud offices.

sentences.zh: 今即江表一隅之地。

translations.literal: Now they hold only a corner of the land south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Now they hold only a corner of the land south of the river.

sentences.zh: 與昔不同，特加矜憫，止令量輸銀一千萬兩以充犒軍之用。

translations.literal: Circumstances differ from the past; showing special compassion, we require only that they contribute ten million taels of silver to serve as army reward.
translations.idiomatic: Circumstances differ from the past; showing special compassion, we require only ten million taels of silver as army reward.

sentences.zh: 方信孺言語反復不足取信，如李大性、硃致知、李璧、吳琯輩似乎忠實，可遣詣軍前稟議。

translations.literal: Fang Xinru's words are inconsistent and not to be trusted; men such as Li Daxing, Zhu Zhizhi, Li Bi, and Wu Guan seem sincere and may be sent to the army to report and deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xinru's words shift back and forth and cannot be trusted; men such as Li Daxing, Zhu Zhizhi, Li Bi, and Wu Guan seem sincere and may be sent to the army to report and deliberate.

sentences.zh: 據方信孺詭詐之罪，過於胡昉，然自古兵交，使人容在其間，姑放令回報。」

translations.literal: Judging by Fang Xinru's crime of deceit, it exceeds that of Hu Fang; yet since ancient times when armies clash, envoys are allowed to pass between them—for now let him be released to return with a reply."
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xinru's deceit exceeds even Hu Fang's; yet since ancient times when armies clash, envoys are permitted to pass between them—for now let him be released to return with a reply."

sentences.zh: 伏遇主上聖德寬裕光大，天覆地容，包荒宥罪，其可不欽承以仰副仁恩之厚！

translations.literal: We bow before our sovereign's sage virtue, broad, luminous, and encompassing heaven and earth, pardoning excess and forgiving crime—how could we not reverently accept it to answer the depth of benevolent grace!
translations.idiomatic: We bow before our sovereign's sage virtue—broad, luminous, covering heaven and earth, pardoning excess and forgiving crime—how could we not reverently accept it to answer such profound benevolent grace!

sentences.zh: 儻猶有所稽違，則和好之事，勿複冀也。

translations.literal: If there is still delay and disobedience, then do not hope again for peace.
translations.idiomatic: If you still delay and disobey, do not hope again for peace.

sentences.zh: 夫宋國之安危存亡，將系於此，更期審慮，無貽後悔！

translations.literal: The safety, peril, survival, or destruction of the Song state will hang on this; we urge you to consider carefully and not bring later regret!
translations.idiomatic: The safety and survival of the Song state will hang on this; consider carefully and do not bring later regret!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金自宗弼渡江而還，既而畫淮為界。

translations.literal: The commentator says: After Jin, since Zongbi crossed the Yangzi and returned, the Huai River was thereafter drawn as the border.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: After Zongbi crossed the Yangzi and returned, the Huai River was drawn as the border.

sentences.zh: 厥後海陵咈眾舉兵，國用虛耗，上下離心，內難先作。

translations.literal: Afterward Hailing defied the multitude and raised armies; state revenues were drained, above and below lost heart, and internal troubles arose first.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Hailing defied popular will and raised armies; state revenues were drained, court and people lost heart, and internal troubles arose first.

sentences.zh: 故世宗之初，章宗之末，有事于南，皆非得已，而詳問之使每先發焉。

translations.literal: Therefore at the beginning of Shizong and the end of Zhangzong, when there was business in the south, it was never without necessity; yet envoys sent to inquire in detail were always dispatched first.
translations.idiomatic: Thus at the beginning of Shizong's reign and the end of Zhangzong's, campaigns in the south were never undertaken lightly—yet envoys sent to inquire in detail were always dispatched first.

sentences.zh: 侂胄狂謀誤國，動非其時，取敗宜也。

translations.literal: Tuozhou's reckless plotting harmed the state; he acted at the wrong time, and defeat was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou's reckless plotting harmed the state; he acted at the wrong time, and defeat was only to be expected.

sentences.zh: 揆、宗浩雖師出輒捷，而行成之使，不拒其來。

translations.literal: Though Kui and Zong Hao won victories whenever their armies marched forth, they did not reject envoys coming to conclude peace.
translations.idiomatic: Though Kui and Zong Hao won whenever their armies marched forth, they did not reject envoys coming to conclude peace.

sentences.zh: 儀幣書辭，抑揚增損之際，有可藉口，即許其平矣。

translations.literal: In ceremonial gifts and written language, at the points of restraint, elevation, addition, or reduction, if there was ground to seize upon, peace was granted at once.
translations.idiomatic: In ceremonial gifts and written language, wherever restraint or elevation, addition or reduction offered a pretext, peace was granted at once.

sentences.zh: 函首之事，宋人亦欲因是以自除其禍耳。

translations.literal: As for the matter of the boxed head, the Song also wished by this means to remove their own calamity.
translations.idiomatic: As for delivering the head in a box, the Song also wished by this means to remove their own calamity.

sentences.zh: 雖然，揆、宗浩常勝之家，史乂搭驍勇之將，三人相繼而死，和議亦成，天意蓋已休息南北之人歟？

translations.literal: Even so, Kui and Zong Hao were of families ever victorious, and Shiguda was a fiercely brave general—yet the three died in succession, and the peace treaty was concluded. Perhaps Heaven had already wished to give rest to the people of north and south?
translations.idiomatic: Even so, Kui and Zong Hao came from ever-victorious houses, and Shiguda was a fiercely brave general—yet all three died in succession, and the peace treaty was concluded. Perhaps Heaven had already wished to give rest to the people of north and south?
